subpoints.short_title: 3 Theorists on Single-Chain Hadith as Ẓann, Beside Qurʾānic Verses
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see al-Shāfiʿī, al-Ghazālī and Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ on single-chain reports yielding probable belief (ẓann), set beside Qurʾān 10:36 and 53:28 on conjecture and 9:101 and 49:6 on verifying reports.
subpoints.takeaway: Classical theorists held that single-chain reports yield probable belief (ẓann), not certainty.
subpoints.title: Quranic Epistemology (Q. 9:101, 10:36) vs. Narrator Grading & Conjecture

items.text: Requires certainty (yaqīn) in religious truth claims.
States that conjecture (ẓann) avails nothing against the truth.
Al-Shāfiʿī distinguishes single-strand (khāṣṣah) reports from universal (ʿāmmah) transmission.
Single-strand (āḥād) reports yield prevailing probability (ẓann), not certainty.
Al-Ghazālī confirms solitary reports do not yield certainty of knowledge.

showcase.note: The Qurʾān contrasts certainty (yaqīn) with conjecture (ẓann), while classical legal theory classifies most hadiths as probabilistic (ẓannī).

subpoints.summary_markdown: Classical Hadith science (*ʿilm al-rijāl*) postulates universal Companion probity (*ʿadālah*) and holds that later critics could retrospectively discern the inner integrity of thousands of deceased transmitters ([Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, *Muqaddimah* Type 23](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/)). By contrast, the Qurʾān states that even the living Prophet did not know Medina's hidden hypocrites ([Qurʾān 9:101](https://quran.com/9/101)), requires objective evidentiary verification over personal status ([Qurʾān 49:6](https://quran.com/49/6); [24:13](https://quran.com/24/13)), and rejects probabilistic conjecture ([Qurʾān 10:36](https://quran.com/10/36); [53:28](https://quran.com/53/28))—the precise epistemic category (*ẓann*) that classical theorists held is yielded by solitary reports (*āḥād*) ([Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, *Muqaddimah* Type 1](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/10/); [al-Ghazālī, *al-Mustaṣfā* 1/107](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/33/107/)).

evidence_items.label: Qurʾān 9:101 ('You Do Not Know Them; We Know Them') vs. Retrospective Narrator Grading (ʿIlm al-Rijāl) and the Tabūk 'Keeper of the Secret' Hadith
evidence_items.content_markdown: Revealed during the late Medinan Tabūk period (9 AH), **[Qurʾān 9:101](https://quran.com/9/101)** declares to the living Prophet: *"And among the people of Medina are those steeped in hypocrisy; **you [O Muhammad] do not know them—We know them**."* Because the Prophet himself could not discern the hidden hypocrisy (*nifāq*) of his own Medinan contemporaries ([Qurʾān 9:101](https://quran.com/9/101)), compilers writing centuries later could neither empirically verify the inner probity (*ʿadālah*) of thousands of deceased transmitters ([Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, *Muqaddimah* Type 23](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/)) nor reconcile this verse with the second-century Tabūk *"Keeper of the Secret"* tradition claiming he gave Ḥudhayfah a comprehensive secret roster of the hypocrites (al-Bayhaqī, [*al-Sunan al-Kubrā* #16336](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/71/16337/); cf. [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2779a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2779a)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ۖ مَرَدُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ ۖ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُم — "And among the people of Medina are those steeped in hypocrisy; you [O Muhammad] do not know them—We know them." (Qurʾān 9:101)

primary_references.label: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ Type 23, p. 105
Al-Bayhaqī, al-Sunan al-Kubrā 8/#16336 (Tabūk 'Keeper of the Secret' Tradition)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ۖ مَرَدُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ ۖ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُم
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: And among the people of Medina are those steeped in hypocrisy; you [O Muhammad] do not know them—We know them.

evidence_items.label: Qurʾān 10:36 and 53:28 Alongside Classical Statements That Single-Chain Reports (Āḥād) Yield Probable Belief (Ẓann)
evidence_items.content_markdown: Whereas **[Qurʾān 10:36](https://quran.com/10/36)** and **[53:28](https://quran.com/53/28)** reject probabilistic conjecture in matters of religious truth (*"Indeed, conjecture [al-ẓann] avails nothing against the truth"*), Sunni Islam's foundational legal and hadith theorists explicitly stated that solitary hadiths (*akhbār al-āḥād*)—which constitute the vast majority of the Hadith corpus—yield only *ẓann*. **Imām al-Shāfiʿī** ([*al-Risālah* pp. 460–461, #1259–1260](https://shamela.ws/book/8180/546)) acknowledged that solitary transmission does not produce comprehensive certainty (*lā anna dhālika iḥāṭah*), **Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī** ([*al-Mustaṣfā* 1/107](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/33/107/)) wrote that *"the solitary report does not yield knowledge, and this is known by necessity,"* and **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*Muqaddimah* Type 1, pp. 28–29](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/10/)) noted that in its intrinsic nature it *"yields nothing but conjecture... and conjecture may err (wa-l-ẓannu qad yukhṭiʾu)."*
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: خَبَرُ الْوَاحِدِ لَا يُفِيدُ الْعِلْمَ، وَهُوَ مَعْلُومٌ بِالضَّرُورَةِ — "The solitary report does not yield knowledge, and this is known by necessity." (Al-Ghazālī, al-Mustaṣfā 1/107)

primary_references.label: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ Type 1, pp. 28–29

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: خَبَرُ الْوَاحِدِ لَا يُفِيدُ الْعِلْمَ، وَهُوَ مَعْلُومٌ بِالضَّرُورَةِ
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: The solitary report does not yield knowledge, and this is known by necessity.

evidence_items.label: Evidentiary Verification of the Claim (Q. 49:6, Q. 24:13, Q. 12:26–28) vs. Reputation-Based Grading of the Person
evidence_items.content_markdown: Rather than validating or discarding reports based solely on biographical classifications, **[Qurʾān 49:6](https://quran.com/49/6)** instructs believers to *"investigate/verify (fa-tabayyanū)"* the factual report itself. Similarly, in the slander incident (*al-Ifk*, **[Qurʾān 24:13](https://quran.com/24/13)**), the Qurʾān declined to accept the uncorroborated testimony of Medinan Companions without four eyewitnesses—stating that in the absence of objective corroboration *"in the sight of God they are the liars"*—just as **[Qurʾān 12:26–28](https://quran.com/12/26-28)** evaluates an aristocrat's accusation against a servant through physical evidence rather than social status.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ — "O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, verify it." (Qurʾān 49:6)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, verify it.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Sunni legal theorists argue by counter-implication (*mafhūm al-mukhālafah*) from [Qurʾān 49:6](https://quran.com/49/6) that the solitary report of an outwardly upright person (*ʿadl*) requires no external verification, and contend that probable conjecture (*ẓann*) suffices for practical law while reaching epistemic certainty when accompanied by communal acceptance (*talaqqī al-ummah bi-l-qabūl*) ([Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, *Muqaddimah* Type 1, pp. 28–29](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/10/)).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The counter-implication reading of [Qurʾān 49:6](https://quran.com/49/6) stands alongside **[Qurʾān 9:101](https://quran.com/9/101)** (*"you do not know them—We know them"*) and **[Qurʾān 24:13](https://quran.com/24/13)**, which illustrate that outward Medinan standing could neither distinguish an *ʿadl* from a hidden hypocrite nor exempt Companions' uncorroborated reports from multi-witness verification. Second, as **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*Muqaddimah* pp. 28–29](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/10/)), **al-Ghazālī** ([*al-Mustaṣfā* 1/107](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/33/107/)), and **al-Shāfiʿī** ([*al-Risālah* pp. 460–461](https://shamela.ws/book/8180/546)) acknowledged, solitary transmission in its intrinsic nature yields only fallible conjecture (*wa-l-ẓannu qad yukhṭiʾu*), which stands in tension with **[Qurʾān 10:36](https://quran.com/10/36)** and **[53:28](https://quran.com/53/28)** (*"conjecture avails nothing against the truth"*).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
#### 1. Epistemic Limits of Biographical Grading (*ʿIlm al-Rijāl*) Under Qurʾān 9:101 and 49:6

Classical Hadith criticism rests on *al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl*: the premise, codified by **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** in his *Muqaddimah* ([Category 23, p. 105](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/)), that compilers writing centuries after the earliest generations could retrospectively audit both the inner moral rectitude (*ʿadālah*) and cognitive precision (*ḍabṭ*) of thousands of deceased transmitters, while treating the entire first generation of Companions as exempt from scrutiny (*ʿadālat al-ṣaḥābah*). From an epistemological standpoint, however, an individual's private sincerity and unrecorded memory cannot be empirically observed across centuries of oral transmission, leaving biographical dictionaries dependent on socially transmitted reputation.

Within Islamic scripture, **[Qurʾān 9:101](https://quran.com/9/101)** directly bounds such retrospective claims by informing the living Prophet during the late Medinan Tabūk campaign (9 AH) that entrenched hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*) resided among the desert Arabs and the population of Medina whom he himself could not identify. This scriptural baseline carries two direct consequences. First, it stands in tension with second-century traditions transmitted via **Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī** (`ʿan ʿUrwah: balaghanā...`) in **al-Bayhaqī's** *al-Sunan al-Kubrā* ([vol. 8, report #16336](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/71/16337/); compare [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2779a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2779a)), which assert that at Tabūk the Prophet imparted a comprehensive secret list of the hypocrites to **Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān** that guided Caliph ʿUmar's funeral attendance. Second, *a fortiori*, if daily interaction and prophetic office did not disclose the inner hypocrisy of Medinan contemporaries, scholars operating centuries later in Iraq, Iran, or Egypt could not verify the internal probity of long-deceased narrators. Consistently, Qurʾānic adjudication evaluates claims through objective evidence rather than personal status: **[Qurʾān 49:6](https://quran.com/49/6)** mandates independent investigation (*fa-tabayyanū*) of a report's factual accuracy, **[Qurʾān 24:13](https://quran.com/24/13)** rejects uncorroborated Companion rumors in the *Ifk* affair without four eyewitnesses, **[Qurʾān 12:26–28](https://quran.com/12/26-28)** resolves an aristocrat's accusation via physical forensic proof, **[Qurʾān 27:27](https://quran.com/27/27)** tests a trusted envoy's report empirically, and **[Qurʾān 4:82](https://quran.com/4/82)** appeals to internal textual coherence over Meccan elite consensus.

#### 2. Probabilistic Conjecture (*Ẓann*) in Solitary Transmission (*Khabar al-Wāḥid*)

This methodological divergence culminates in the epistemic classification of solitary reports (*akhbār al-āḥād*). While **[Qurʾān 53:28](https://quran.com/53/28)** and **[10:36](https://quran.com/10/36)** state that conjecture (*al-ẓann*) avails nothing against the truth (*al-ḥaqq*), Sunni legal theorists (*uṣūliyyūn*) conceded that solitary hadiths—which constitute almost the entire canonical Hadith corpus—produce only probabilistic *ẓann* rather than comprehensive certainty (*ʿilm* or *iḥāṭah*). **Imām al-Shāfiʿī** in *al-Risālah* ([paras. 1259–1260, pp. 460–461](https://shamela.ws/book/8180/546); cf. [IslamWeb *ʿIlm al-Ḥadīth Dirāyah*](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1516/692/)) analogized solitary transmission to courtroom witness testimony that binds action without yielding inner certainty; **Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī** in *al-Mustaṣfā* ([vol. 1, p. 107](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/33/107/)) declared it self-evident by necessity that solitary reports do not yield knowledge; and **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** in *Muqaddimah* ([pages 28–29, Category 1](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/10/)) acknowledged that in its intrinsic origin a solitary report yields only fallible conjecture (`wa-l-ẓannu qad yukhṭiʾu`).

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: أَجْمَعَ جَمَاهِيرُ أَئِمَّةِ الْحَدِيثِ وَالْفِقْهِ عَلَى أَنَّهُ يُشْتَرَطُ فِيمَنْ يُحْتَجُّ بِرِوَايَتِهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَدْلًا ضَابِطًا لِمَا يَرْوِيهِ، وَتَفْصِيلُهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُسْلِمًا، بَالِغًا، عَاقِلًا، سَالِمًا مِنْ أَسْبَابِ الْفِسْقِ وَخَوَارِمِ الْمُرُوءَةِ...
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "The majority of the imams of hadith and jurisprudence have agreed that it is required of one whose transmission is cited as proof that he be morally upright (ʿadl) and precise (ḍābiṭ) in what he narrates—specifically, that he be a Muslim, of age, of sound mind, and free from the causes of moral transgression (fisq) and defects that undermine personal honor (muruʾah)..."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Type 23, p. 105

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَعْرَابِ مُنَٰفِقُونَ ۖ وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ۖ مَرَدُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ ۖ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُمْ ۚ سَنُعَذِّبُهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ عَظِيمٍ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And among the Bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina are those steeped in hypocrisy; you [O Muhammad] do not know them—We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a great punishment."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ غَزَا تَبُوكَ نَزَلَ عَنْ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَأُوحِيَ إِلَيْهِ وَرَاحِلَتُهُ بَارِكَةٌ، فَقَامَتْ تَجُرُّ زِمَامَهَا حَتَّى لَقِيَهَا حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ الْيَمَانِ... قَالَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «فَإِنِّي أُسِرُّ إِلَيْكَ أَمْرًا فَلَا تَذْكُرَنَّهُ، إِنِّي قَدْ نُهِيتُ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ عَلَى فُلَانٍ وَفُلَانٍ» رَهْطٍ ذَوِي عَدَدٍ مِنَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ، لَمْ يُعْلِمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ذِكْرَهُمْ لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِ حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ الْيَمَانِ، فَلَمَّا تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فِي خِلَافَتِهِ إِذَا مَاتَ رَجُلٌ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ مِنْ أُولَئِكَ الرَّهْطِ، أَخَذَ بِيَدِ حُذَيْفَةَ فَاقْتَادَهُ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ عَلَيْهِ، فَإِنْ مَشَى مَعَهُ حُذَيْفَةُ صَلَّى عَلَيْهِ، وَإِنِ انْتَزَعَ حُذَيْفَةُ يَدَهُ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَمْشِيَ مَعَهُ انْصَرَفَ عُمَرُ مَعَهُ فَأَبَى أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ...
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "From ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: 'It reached us (balaghanā) that when the Messenger of God ﷺ marched to Tabūk, he dismounted from his riding camel, and revelation came to him while his camel was kneeling... The Messenger of God ﷺ said [to Ḥudhayfah]: "I am confiding a secret to you, so do not mention it: I have been forbidden to pray [the funeral prayer] over so-and-so and so-and-so"—a specific group of hypocrites whose names the Messenger of God ﷺ did not make known to anyone other than Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān. When the Messenger of God ﷺ passed away, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb during his caliphate, whenever a man died whom he suspected of belonging to that group, would take Ḥudhayfah by the hand and lead him to the funeral prayer; if Ḥudhayfah walked with him, he would pray over him, and if Ḥudhayfah pulled his hand back and refused to go, ʿUmar would turn away with him and refuse to pray over him...'"
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Al-Bayhaqī, al-Sunan al-Kubrā 8/#16336; cf. Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2779a–c

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَٰلَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَٰدِمِينَ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one (fāsiq) with information, investigate/verify it (fa-tabayyanū), lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى ۚ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ ۝ وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "He [Joseph] said, 'It was she who sought to seduce me.' And a witness from her family testified: 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.'"

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: قَالَ سَنَنظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "[Solomon] said, 'We will see whether you have spoken the truth or are of the liars.'"

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَٰفًا كَثِيرًا
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Then do they not reflect upon the Qurʾān? If it had been from [any] other than God, they would have found within it much contradiction."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا ۚ إِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And most of them follow nothing but conjecture (ẓann). Indeed, conjecture (al-ẓann) avails nothing against the truth (al-ḥaqq). Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ ۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And they have thereof no knowledge (ʿilm). They follow not except conjecture (al-ẓann), and indeed, conjecture avails not against the truth at all."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: فَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ سُنَّةٍ مِنْ خَبَرِ الْخَاصَّةِ الَّذِي قَدْ يَخْتَلِفُ الْخَبَرُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ الْخَبَرُ مُحْتَمِلًا لِلتَّأْوِيلِ وَجَاءَ الْخَبَرُ فِيهِ مِنْ طَرِيقِ الِانْفِرَادِ، فَالْحُجَّةُ فِيهِ عِنْدِي أَنْ يَلْزَمَ الْعَالِمِينَ حَتَّى لَا يَكُونَ لَهُمْ رَدُّ مَا كَانَ مَنْصُوصًا مِنْهُ، كَمَا يَلْزَمُهُمْ أَنْ يَقْبَلُوا شَهَادَةَ الْعُدُولِ، لَا أَنَّ ذَلِكَ إِحَاطَةٌ كَمَا يَكُونُ نَصُّ الْكِتَابِ وَخَبَرُ الْعَامَّةِ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "As for a Sunnah derived from a solitary report (khabar al-khāṣṣah) concerning which reports may differ, so that the report is open to interpretation and has come by way of isolated transmission (ṭarīq al-infirād): the proof in it, in my view, is that it binds scholars such that they may not reject what is explicitly stated in it—just as they are bound to accept the testimony of outwardly upright witnesses (shahādat al-ʿudūl)—not that this constitutes comprehensive certainty (lā anna dhālika iḥāṭah) in the manner of the text of the Book and the general report (khabar al-ʿāmmah) from the Messenger of God ﷺ."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَإِذَا عَرَفْتَ هَذَا فَنَقُولُ: خَبَرُ الْوَاحِدِ لَا يُفِيدُ الْعِلْمَ، وَهُوَ مَعْلُومٌ بِالضَّرُورَةِ؛ فَإِنَّا لَا نُصَدِّقُ بِكُلِّ مَا نَسْمَعُ، وَلَوْ صَدَّقْنَا وَقَدَّرْنَا تَعَارُضَ خَبَرَيْنِ فَكَيْفَ نُصَدِّقُ بِالضِّدَّيْنِ؟ وَمَا حُكِيَ عَنِ الْمُحَدِّثِينَ مِنْ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ يُوجِبُ الْعِلْمَ فَلَعَلَّهُمْ أَرَادُوا أَنَّهُ يُفِيدُ الْعِلْمَ بِوُجُوبِ الْعَمَلِ؛ إِذْ يُسَمَّى الظَّنُّ عِلْمًا...
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Once you understand this, we say: The solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid) does not yield knowledge (lā yufīdu al-ʿilm), and this is known by necessity (maʿlūm bi-l-ḍarūrah); for we do not hold as certain everything we hear, and if we did so and posited a contradiction between two reports, how could we hold two opposites to be true? As for what is related from the hadith folk (al-muḥaddithīn) that it necessitates knowledge, perhaps they meant that it yields knowledge of the obligation to act, since conjecture (al-ẓann) is [figuratively] called knowledge..."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَهَذَا الْقِسْمُ جَمِيعُهُ مَقْطُوعٌ بِصِحَّتِهِ وَالْعِلْمُ الْيَقِينِيُّ النَّظَرِيُّ وَاقِعٌ بِهِ. خِلَافًا لِقَوْلِ مَنْ نَفَى ذَلِكَ، مُحْتَجًّا بِأَنَّهُ لَا يُفِيدُ فِي أَصْلِهِ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ، وَإِنَّمَا تَلَقَّتْهُ الْأُمَّةُ بِالْقَبُولِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعَمَلُ بِالظَّنِّ، وَالظَّنُّ قَدْ يُخْطِئُ. وَقَدْ كُنْتُ أَمِيلُ إِلَى هَذَا وَأَحْسَبُهُ قَوِيًّا...
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And this category in its entirety is affirmed as sound, and theoretical certain knowledge occurs through it—contrary to the view of those who denied that, arguing that in its origin it yields nothing but conjecture (lā yufīdu fī aṣlihi illā al-ẓann), and that the community only received it with acceptance because they are obligated to act upon conjecture, and conjecture may err (wa-l-ẓannu qad yukhṭiʾu). And I myself used to incline toward this view and consider it strong..."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, Type 1, pp. 28–29

subpoints.short_title: Omitting a Link (Tadlīs) in the Ṣaḥīḥs and 3 Critics Who Questioned It
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see narrators in both Ṣaḥīḥs whom Ibn Ḥajar ranked as mudallisūn (omitting an intermediary), Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ's presumption that their hearing was verified, and 3 Mamluk specialists who called it assumption.
subpoints.takeaway: Later scholars presumed hearing was verified in these two books; some Mamluk specialists called it assumption.
subpoints.title: How Scholars Treated 'From' (Muʿanʿan) Links by Mudallis Narrators in the Ṣaḥīḥayn

showcase.note: Second-century transmitters known for omitting intermediate links (tadlīs) are accepted inside Bukhārī and Muslim on the presumption that the compilers verified their sources.

narrators.name: Al-Zuhrī / Qatādah / al-Aʿmash
narrators.verdict: Ranked as mudallisūn who sometimes omitted intermediate narrators when saying 'from' (ʿan)

narrators.name: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī & Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim
narrators.verdict: Ambiguous ('from') chains inside the Ṣaḥīḥayn are accepted on the presumption of prior verification

subpoints.summary_markdown: Several primary regional 'common link' transmitters in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* were documented practitioners of *tadlīs* (omission of intermediaries), transmitting canonical reports via ambiguous *ʿan* ('from') phrasing without explicit verification of direct hearing in those specific narrations (**Ibn Ḥajar**, [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* pp. 13–51](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30); [*al-Nukat* 2/636–644](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/615)). While post-canonical theorists such as **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* p. 75](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/)) and **al-Nawawī** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/145](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/103/)) proposed a methodological exemption exclusively for the *Ṣaḥīḥayn*—positing that direct hearing had been verified via unrecorded external pathways—Mamluk Hadith specialists including **Ibn al-Muraḥḥal**, **Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd**, and **al-Mizzī** concluded that this rule rested on charitable assumption (*taḥsīn al-ẓann*) rather than documented evidence (**Ibn Ḥajar**, [*al-Nukat* 2/635–636](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/609)).

evidence_items.label: Mamluk Hadith Specialists Evaluating the Post-Canonical 'Unrecorded Pathway' Exemption
evidence_items.content_markdown: When **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* p. 75](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/)) and **al-Nawawī** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/145](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/103/)) argued that ambiguous *ʿan* chains of *mudallisūn* in *Bukhārī* and *Muslim* had their direct hearing (*samāʿ*) verified via unrecorded external pathways, three Mamluk Hadith specialists quoted in **Ibn Ḥajar's** [*al-Nukat* (2/635–636)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/609) critiqued this premise. **Ibn al-Muraḥḥal** (d. 716 AH) characterized it as *"an assertion with no evidence for it (daʿwā lā dalīla ʿalayhā),"* **Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd** (d. 702 AH) described it as *"a referral to an unknown (iḥālah ʿalā jahālah),"* and **Jamāl al-Dīn al-Mizzī** (d. 742 AH) acknowledged that it rested on *"charitable assumption (taḥsīn al-ẓann)"* because numerous *muʿanʿan* reports of *mudallisūn* in the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* are not attested via any other pathway ([*al-Nukat* 2/636](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/610)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: إما أن يدعى أن تلك الأحاديث عرف صاحب الصحيح صحة السماع فيها قال وهذا إحالة على جهالة وإثبات أمر بمجرد الاحتمال — "Either it is claimed that the author of the Ṣaḥīḥ knew those hadiths were heard [without tadlīs]—but this is referring to the unknown, and affirming a matter by mere possibility." (Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat 2/635)

primary_references.label: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth (Muqaddimah), Type 12, p. 75
Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat ʿalā Kitāb Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ 2/635–636 (Critiques by Ibn al-Muraḥḥal, Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd, and al-Mizzī)

key_arabic_quote_structured.english: Either it is claimed that the author of the Ṣaḥīḥ knew those hadiths were heard [without tadlīs]—but this is referring to the unknown, and affirming a matter by mere possibility.

evidence_items.label: Prolific Rank 2 and Rank 3 Mudallisūn Serving as Primary Transmitters in the Ṣaḥīḥayn
evidence_items.content_markdown: Although **Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj** (d. 160 AH) condemned *tadlīs* as *"the brother of lying"* and more severe than fornication (**Ibn Abī Ḥātim**, [*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 1/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/200)), **Ibn Ḥajar** documents in [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* (pp. 13–47)](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30) and [*al-Nukat* (2/636–644)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/615) that several central regional pivots of the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* were frequent practitioners of *tadlīs*. These include **Sufyān al-Thawrī**, **Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah**, **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī**, and **Sulaymān al-Aʿmash** (classified in Rank 3 in [*al-Nukat* 2/640](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/614) and Rank 2 in [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* p. 33](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30)), alongside Rank 3 *mudallisūn* (whose *ʿan* chains are methodologically rejected outside the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* without explicit hearing) such as **Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī**, **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah**, **Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī**, **Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī**, and **Hushaym ibn Bashīr** ([*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* pp. 37–47](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/39)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: لأن أزني أحب إلي من أن أدلس — "To commit fornication is dearer to me than to commit tadlīs." (Al-Jarḥ wa-al-Taʿdīl 1/173)

primary_references.label: Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 1/173 (Shuʿbah on Tadlīs)
Ibn Ḥajar, Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs pp. 13–47
Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat ʿalā Kitāb Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ 2/636–644 (Ranks of Mudallisūn)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: لأن أزني أحب إلى من أن أدلس
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: To commit fornication is dearer to me than to commit tadlīs.

evidence_items.label: Severe Tadlīs (Ibn Jurayj) and Tadlīs al-Taswiyah (al-Walīd ibn Muslim) Inside the Ṣaḥīḥayn
evidence_items.content_markdown: Regarding the Meccan pivot **Ibn Jurayj** (whose narrations appear across all Six Books), **al-Dāraquṭnī** stated in [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* (6/405)](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/2713) and [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* (#83, p. 41)](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/39) that his *tadlīs* was *"reprehensible (qabīḥ al-tadlīs); he only commits tadlīs in what he heard from a disparaged narrator (majrūḥ), such as Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā."* Furthermore, **al-Walīd ibn Muslim**—classified by **Ibn Ḥajar** in Rank 4 for severe *tadlīs* ([*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* #127, p. 51](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/49)), while his *tadlīs al-taswiyah* (dropping weak teachers of al-Awzāʿī) is documented in [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* (11/154)](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/4937)—transmits from al-Awzāʿī via ambiguous *ʿan* and *qāla* chains inside the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* (e.g., [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 897c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:897c), [901d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901d)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: تجنب تدليس ابن جريج فإنه قبيح التدليس لا يدلس إلا فيما سمعه من مجروح — "Avoid Ibn Jurayj's tadlīs; he only conceals what he heard from a disparaged narrator." (Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 6/405)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Traditional commentators and Hadith theorists—such as **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* p. 75](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/)) and **al-Nawawī** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/145](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/103/))—maintain that *mudallisūn* whose *muʿanʿan* reports appear in the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* either belong to the lenient second tier (whose *tadlīs* was infrequent relative to their total transmissions, as categorized in **Ibn Ḥajar's** [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* pp. 13–36](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30)) or had their direct hearing (*samāʿ*) independently verified by al-Bukhārī and Muslim via auxiliary pathways not recorded in their collections.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Several primary canonical transmitters—including al-Zuhrī, Qatādah, Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, and Ibn Jurayj—are classified in the third tier of *mudallisūn* (whose *ʿan* transmissions require explicit proof of hearing), and al-Walīd ibn Muslim is placed in the fourth tier, in **Ibn Ḥajar's** [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* (pp. 37–51)](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/39), alongside al-Aʿmash's placement in the third tier in [*al-Nukat* (2/640)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/614). Furthermore, Mamluk authorities **Ibn al-Muraḥḥal**, **Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd**, and **al-Mizzī** ([*al-Nukat* 2/635–636](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/609)) evaluated the 'unrecorded pathway' hypothesis enacted by **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* p. 75](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/)) and concluded that it lacked empirical verification, as numerous *muʿanʿan* reports in the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* are unattested through any alternative chain.

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
#### 1. Structural Mechanics of *Tadlīs al-Isnād* and *Tadlīs al-Taswiyah*

In classical Hadith nomenclature—codified in **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ's** [*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* (pp. 73–74)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/) and **Ibn Ḥajar's** [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* (p. 16)](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/12)—omission of intermediaries (*tadlīs*) operates through two primary mechanisms. In *tadlīs al-isnād*, a transmitter drops his immediate informant and cites an earlier contemporary authority whom he had met using ambiguous terms such as *ʿan* ("from"), creating the appearance of direct audition without uttering a technical falsehood. In *tadlīs al-taswiyah*, a narrator retains his own immediate reliable teacher but excises a weak or disparaged link higher up between two trustworthy authorities who were contemporaries. Because both practices conceal broken links and shield impugned intermediaries from detection, **Shuʿbah** (d. 160 AH) denounced *tadlīs* in the strongest moral terms across early critical treatises ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 1/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/200); [*al-Kifāyah* pp. 355–356](https://shamela.ws/book/13055/1319); [*Siyar* 7/210](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/1184/); [*Fatḥ al-Mughīth* 1/234–235](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/82/64/)).

#### 2. Stratification of Canonical Pivots Across Ranks 2, 3, and 4

When **Ibn Ḥajar** stratified known practitioners of *tadlīs* into five tiers in [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* (pp. 13–14)](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30) and [p. 14](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/10) alongside [*al-Nukat* (2/636–644)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/615), many of the most prolific regional common links of *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* fell within Tiers 2 through 4. Tier 2 encompasses **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** ([#40, p. 29](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/26)), **Sufyān al-Thawrī** and **Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah** ([#51–52, p. 32](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/29)), and **Sulaymān al-Aʿmash** ([#55, p. 33](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30)), whom Ibn Ḥajar had previously assigned to Tier 3 in [*al-Nukat* (2/640, #37)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/614) ([IslamWeb 313/150](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/313/150/)). Tier 3—whose non-explicit *ʿan* chains are methodologically inadmissible under standard rules—contains foundational canonical pivots including **Ibn Jurayj** ([#83, p. 41](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/39); [*al-Nukat* 2/641](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/615); [*Tahdhīb* 6/405](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/2713)), **Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī** ([#91, p. 42](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/40)), **Qatādah** ([#92, p. 43](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/41)), **Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī** and **al-Zuhrī** ([#101–102, p. 45](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/43); [*al-Nukat* 2/642](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/616)), and **Hushaym ibn Bashīr** ([#111, p. 47](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/45); [*al-Nukat* 2/643](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/617)). Even Tier 4 includes **Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd** ([#117, p. 49](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/47)) and **al-Walīd ibn Muslim** ([#127, p. 51](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/49); [*Tahdhīb* 11/154](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/4937)), whose *ʿan* and *qāla* narrations from al-Awzāʿī appear in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 897c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:897c) and [901d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901d).

#### 3. Mamluk Hadith Specialists on the Ṣaḥīḥayn Presumption

Because the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* contain numerous *ʿan* narrations from prolific *mudallisūn* like Qatādah and al-Aʿmash (**Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ**, [*ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* p. 75](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/42/)), later authorities codified an institutional exemption for these collections: `«وَمَا كَانَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَشِبْهِهِمَا مِنَ الْكُتُبِ الصَّحِيحَةِ عَنِ الْمُدَلِّسِينَ بِعَنْ فَمَحْمُولٌ عَلَى ثُبُوتِ السَّمَاعِ»` ([*Tadrīb al-Rāwī* 1/263](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/88/145/)), while comparing the narrator precision and chain continuity of *al-Bukhārī* and *Muslim* ([*Hady al-Sārī* pp. 11–12](https://shamela.ws/book/1673/9)). However, as documented in [*al-Nukat* (2/635–636)](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/609), Mamluk theorists **Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd**, **Ibn al-Muraḥḥal**, and **al-Mizzī** pointed out that this presumption reverses the burden of proof: rather than authenticating the book through verified chains, it authenticates unverified chains through the prestige of the book.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: قَالَ الشَّافِعِيُّ: قَالَ شُعْبَةُ: «التَّدْلِيسُ أَخُو الْكَذِبِ». قَالَ شُعْبَةُ: «لَأَنْ أَزْنِيَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُدَلِّسَ».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: Al-Shāfiʿī said: Shuʿbah said: "Tadlīs is the brother of lying." Shuʿbah also said: "To commit fornication [zinā] is dearer to me than to commit tadlīs."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī, al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 1/173; al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī, al-Kifāyah pp. 355–356; Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth pp. 74–75; al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ 7/210.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَقَالَ الدَّارَقُطْنِيُّ: «تَجَنَّبْ تَدْلِيسَ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ فَإِنَّهُ قَبِيحُ التَّدْلِيسِ، لَا يُدَلِّسُ إِلَّا فِيمَا سَمِعَهُ مِنْ مَجْرُوحٍ، مِثْلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي يَحْيَى وَمُوسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدَةَ وَغَيْرِهِمَا».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: Al-Dāraquṭnī said: "Avoid the tadlīs of Ibn Jurayj, for his tadlīs is reprehensible [qabīḥ al-tadlīs]; he only commits tadlīs in what he heard from a disparaged narrator [majrūḥ], such as Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā, Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, and others besides them."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 6/405 and Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs, p. 41 (#83).

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «وَمَا كَانَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَشِبْهِهِمَا عَنِ الْمُدَلِّسِينَ بِعَنْ، فَهُوَ مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى ثُبُوتِ السَّمَاعِ مِنْ جِهَةٍ أُخْرَى».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And whatever occurs in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs and their like from the mudallisūn with 'ʿan' [from] is to be construed as having established direct hearing [samāʿ] through another pathway."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth, Type 12, p. 75; al-Nawawī, Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1/145; Ibn Ḥajar, Hady al-Sārī pp. 11–12.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «لِأَنَّهَا دَعْوَى لَا دَلِيلَ عَلَيْهَا، لَا سِيَّمَا أَنَّا قَدْ وَجَدْنَا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْحُفَّاظِ يُعَلِّلُونَ أَحَادِيثَ وَقَعَتْ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا بِتَدْلِيسِ رُوَاتِهَا».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Because it is an assertion with no evidence for it [daʿwā lā dalīla ʿalayhā]—especially since we have found many of the hadith masters [ḥuffāẓ] diagnosing as defective [yuʿallilūna] hadiths that occurred in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs, or in one of them, on account of the tadlīs of their narrators."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ṣadr al-Dīn Ibn al-Muraḥḥal (Ibn al-Wakīl), in Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat ʿalā Kitāb Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ 2/635.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «وَهَذَا إِحَالَةٌ عَلَى جَهَالَةٍ، وَإِثْبَاتُ أَمْرٍ بِمُجَرَّدِ الِاحْتِمَالِ، وَلَوْ صَحَّ هَذَا لَمْ يَبْقَ لَنَا طَرِيقٌ إِلَى النَّظَرِ فِي تَصْحِيحِهِمَا».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "This is a referral to an unknown [iḥālah ʿalā jahālah] and the establishment of a matter by mere possibility [bi-mujarrad al-iḥtimāl]; and if this were valid, there would remain no pathway for us to critically examine their authentication."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd, al-Iqtirāḥ, quoted in Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat ʿalā Kitāb Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ 2/635.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: وَحَكَى العَلَائِيُّ عَنْ شَيْخِهِ الحَافِظِ أَبِي الحَجَّاجِ المِزِّيِّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «كَذَا يَقُولُونَ، وَمَا فِيهِ إِلَّا تَحْسِينُ الظَّنِّ بِهِمَا، وَإِلَّا فَفِيهِمَا أَحَادِيثُ مِنْ رِوَايَةِ الْمُدَلِّسِينَ مَا تُوجَدُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تِلْكَ الطَّرِيقِ الَّتِي فِي الصَّحِيحِ».
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: Al-ʿAlāʾī related from his teacher, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Ḥajjāj al-Mizzī, that he said: "That is what they say, yet there is nothing in it except holding a charitable assumption [taḥsīn al-ẓann] toward the two of them [al-Bukhārī and Muslim]; otherwise, there are hadiths in the two of them from the narration of mudallisūn that are not found via any pathway other than that very pathway which is in the Ṣaḥīḥ."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Mizzī, in Ibn Ḥajar, al-Nukat ʿalā Kitāb Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ 2/636 (https://shamela.ws/book/8316/610); al-Suyūṭī, Tadrīb al-Rāwī 1/263.

subpoints.short_title: Imām Muslim on Whether Narrators Must Meet, and 2 Chains Examined
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see Imām Muslim's introduction accepting contemporaries without a recorded meeting, al-Bukhārī's reported stricter rule, and two chains where classical scholars questioned whether the narrators met.
subpoints.takeaway: Al-Bukhārī is reported to have required a meeting; Imām Muslim held that contemporaries suffice for a chain.
subpoints.title: Muslim's Muqaddimah on Contemporaneity (*Muʿāṣarah*) vs. Verified Meeting (*Liqāʾ*)

showcase.note: Al-Bukhārī required proof that a teacher and student met at least once (liqāʾ). Muslim accepted any unbroken chain provided the two merely lived in the same century (muʿāṣarah).

subpoints.summary_markdown: In his methodological introduction, **Imām Muslim** ([*Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/30](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1/75/)) explicitly rejects the requirement of proving that a narrator physically met his teacher (*thubūt al-liqāʾ*), stating that the consensus of Hadith scholars accepted ambiguous *ʿan* ('from') chains based on contemporaneity (*imkān al-liqāʾ*) without any record of face-to-face contact. Classical biographical and commentary testimonies further document canonical chains in which compilers omitted disparaged intermediaries—such as **Imām Mālik** omitting **ʿIkrimah** between **Thawr ibn Zayd** and **Ibn ʿAbbās** (**al-Mizzī**, who explicitly states in [*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* (4/416)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/906/) that Thawr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās "and did not reach/meet him" (`وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَلَمْ يُدْرِكْهُ`); and **Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr**, who discusses Mālik dropping ʿIkrimah in [*al-Tamhīd* (2/26)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/78/82/); [*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 24/5](https://sunnah.com/malik:24/5))—or transmitted reports through narrators attested by familial testimony not to have heard from the cited Companion, as in the `Abū Ḥāzim ← Abū Hurayrah` strand (**al-Mizzī**, [*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 11/275](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/2640/); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3237](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3237)).

evidence_items.label: Imām Muslim's Critique of the 'Verified Meeting (Liqāʾ)' Requirement as an Unprecedented Innovation
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (1/30)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1/75/), **Imām Muslim** critiques the condition later associated with al-Bukhārī and ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī (**Ibn Rajab**, [*Sharḥ ʿIlal al-Tirmidhī* 1/365–367](https://shamela.ws/book/9552/312))—that an ambiguous *ʿan* chain requires positive proof that student and teacher met at least once (*thubūt al-liqāʾ*)—characterizing it as an unprecedented innovation (*qawl mukhtaraʿ mustaḥdath*). He states that the established consensus of earlier and later Hadith scholars accepted any *ʿan* chain between trustworthy contemporaries (*imkān al-liqāʾ*), *"even if no report has ever come down stating that they ever met or spoke face-to-face"* ([*Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/30](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1/75/)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: وإن لم يأت في خبر قط أنهما اجتمعا ولا تشافها بكلام — "Even if no report ever states that they met or spoke face-to-face." (Muslim Intro 1/30)

primary_references.label: Imām Muslim, Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1/30 (Critique of the Liqāʾ Criterion)
Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī, Sharḥ ʿIlal al-Tirmidhī 1/365–367 (Discussion of the Liqāʾ Condition)

evidence_items.label: Canonical Bukhārī 3237 and Muslim 1436d Chains Disavowed by Familial Testimony on Abū Ḥāzim ← Abū Hurayrah
evidence_items.content_markdown: In **al-Mizzī's** [*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* (11/275)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/2640/) and **al-Dhahabī's** [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* (6/96–97)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/954/), the jurist **ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Ḥāzim** (d. 184 AH)—son of the Medinan Successor **Abū Ḥāzim Salamah ibn Dīnār**—attested: *"Whoever told you that my father heard from any of the Companions other than Sahl ibn Saʿd has spoken falsely."* Notwithstanding this testimony, [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3237](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3237), [5193](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5193), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1436d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1436d) transmit canonical rulings via an unqualified `al-Aʿmash ← Abū Ḥāzim ← Abū Hurayrah` chain.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ فَبَاتَ غَضْبَانَ عَلَيْهَا لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ — "When a man invites his wife to his bed and she refuses, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning [transmitted via al-Aʿmash ← Abū Ḥāzim ← Abū Hurayrah]." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3237 (cf. Tahdhīb al-Kamāl 11/275))

evidence_items.label: Imām Mālik's Testimony on Thawr ibn Zayd ← Ibn ʿAbbās and the Omission of ʿIkrimah in the Muwaṭṭaʾ
evidence_items.content_markdown: Asked by Bishr ibn ʿUmar whether **Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dīlī** (d. 135 AH) ever met **Ibn ʿAbbās** (d. 68 AH), **Imām Mālik** stated, *"No, he never met him"* (**al-ʿAlāʾī**, [*Tuḥfat al-Taḥṣīl* 1/55, #116](https://shamela.ws/narrator/1079)), and **al-Mizzī** likewise notes that Thawr *"did not reach his lifetime (wa-lam yudrikhu)"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 4/416–417](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/906/)), yet Mālik included four *Muwaṭṭaʾ* reports with the direct chain `Mālik ← Thawr ← Ibn ʿAbbās` ([*Muwaṭṭaʾ* 18/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:18), [20/156](https://sunnah.com/malik:20), [24/5](https://sunnah.com/malik:24/5), [30/4](https://sunnah.com/malik:30/4)). In [*al-Tamhīd* (2/26)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/78/82/), **Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr** notes that Thawr received these reports via the disparaged intermediary **ʿIkrimah**, whom Mālik omitted from the *isnād* because he disapproved of having ʿIkrimah named in his compilation due to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab's criticism of him.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: أَنَّ مَالِكًا أَسْقَطَ ذِكْرَ عِكْرِمَةَ مِنْهُ لِأَنَّهُ كَرِهَ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي كِتَابِهِ لِكَلَامِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ — "They maintained that Mālik dropped the mention of ʿIkrimah from it because he disliked having him in his book on account of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab's criticisms." (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, al-Tamhīd 2/26 (cf. Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik 24/5))

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Traditional commentators and Hadith theorists maintain that al-Bukhārī enforced the stricter physical-meeting requirement (*thubūt al-liqāʾ*) throughout his *Ṣaḥīḥ* (**Ibn Rajab**, [*Sharḥ ʿIlal al-Tirmidhī* 1/365–367](https://shamela.ws/book/9552/312)), and clarify that the 'Abū Ḥāzim' appearing in the `al-Aʿmash ← Abū Ḥāzim ← Abū Hurayrah` strand of [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3237](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3237) and [5193](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5193) is not the Medinan Salamah ibn Dīnār ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 11/275](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/2640/)), but rather a Kufan Successor of the same *kunyah*, Salmān al-Ashjaʿī.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: **Imām Muslim's** [*Muqaddimah* (1/30)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1/75/) attests that earlier Hadith scholars did not require positive proof of physical meeting—indicating that the pre-Bukhārian corpus was compiled under the broader contemporaneity standard—while **Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī** compiled a dedicated treatise (*Bayān Khaṭaʾ Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī fī Tārīkhihi* p. 9; cf. **Ibn Rajab**, [*Sharḥ ʿIlal al-Tirmidhī* 1/365–367](https://shamela.ws/book/9552/312)) documenting instances where Abū Ḥātim and Abū Zurʿah corrected al-Bukhārī's biographical inferences regarding narrator meetings. Furthermore, identifying the transmitter in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3237](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3237) and [5193](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5193) as the Kufan Salmān al-Ashjaʿī still leaves the report dependent on the ambiguous *ʿan* transmission of **Sulaymān al-Aʿmash**, a documented practitioner of *tadlīs* (**Ibn Ḥajar**, [*al-Nukat* 2/640](https://shamela.ws/book/8316/614); [*Taʿrīf Ahl al-Taqdīs* p. 33](https://shamela.ws/book/1186/30)).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
#### 1. Contemporaneity (*Muʿāṣarah*) vs. Verified Physical Contact (*Liqāʾ*)

In the methodological treatise opening his collection ([*Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1/30](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1/75/); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* Introduction](https://sunnah.com/muslim:introduction)), **Imām Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj** (d. 261 AH) argues at length against the requirement—associated with his teacher al-Bukhārī and ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī—that an ambiguous *ʿan* ("from") chain cannot be accepted unless historical evidence shows that student and teacher met in person at least once. He asserts instead that scholars of reports generally accepted any such chain provided the two individuals lived contemporaneously (*imkān al-liqāʾ*), whether or not formal documentation of a meeting exists.

Historically, this debate highlights key methodological differences in early *isnād* evaluation. First, throughout the formative period prior to al-Bukhārī, *muʿanʿan* chains were routinely accepted as continuous solely on the basis of overlapping lifespans. Furthermore, researchers such as **Christopher Melchert** (2001) note that when third-century scholars sought to establish physical encounters in works like *al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr*, they frequently deduced these meetings directly from the *isnād* structures themselves rather than external archives—a process prone to prosopographical errors that **Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī** cataloged in his *Bayān Khaṭaʾ al-Bukhārī* (p. 9).

#### 2. Editorial Omission of Disparaged Links in the *Muwaṭṭaʾ*

The divergence between apparent chain continuity and underlying historical transmission is illustrated by the strand `Mālik → Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dīlī → Ibn ʿAbbās`. Although **al-Mizzī** ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 4/416–417](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/906/)) and **al-ʿAlāʾī** ([*Tuḥfat al-Taḥṣīl* #116](https://shamela.ws/narrator/1079)) record **Imām Mālik's** acknowledgment to **Bishr ibn ʿUmar** that Thawr ibn Zayd (d. 135 AH) never reached or met Ibn ʿAbbās (d. 68 AH), Mālik transmitted legal traditions via that direct chain in [*Muwaṭṭaʾ* 18/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:18), [20/156](https://sunnah.com/malik:20), [24/5](https://sunnah.com/malik:24/5), and [30/4](https://sunnah.com/malik:30/4), while retaining the intermediary ʿIkrimah in [20/165](https://sunnah.com/malik:20). In [*al-Tamhīd* (2/26)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/78/82/) (cf. [2/1–2](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/78/79/)), **Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr** explains that Thawr had received these reports through Ibn ʿAbbās's controversial freedman **ʿIkrimah**, whose name was dropped from the *Muwaṭṭaʾ* chains because Mālik disapproved of citing him due to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab's criticisms.

#### 3. Filial Disavowal of Canonical Companion Links

A parallel gap appears in the canonical marital-refusal tradition transmitted in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3237](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3237), [5193](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5193), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1436d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1436d) via `al-Aʿmash → Abū Ḥāzim → Abū Hurayrah`. In [*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* (11/275)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/2640/) and [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* (6/96–97)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/954/), Medinan legal authority **ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Ḥāzim** testified that his father Salamah ibn Dīnār never heard from any Companion except Sahl ibn Saʿd. While classical commentators reassign the *kunyah* in this chain to the Kufan freedman Salmān al-Ashjaʿī, the report's continuity remains dependent on the unspecified *ʿan* phrasing of the Kufan *mudallis* Sulaymān al-Aʿmash. The methodological divide between al-Bukhārī and Muslim illustrates that the two premier canonical collections rest upon different criteria for establishing continuity.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «وَهَذَا الْقَوْلُ، يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ، فِي الطَّعْنِ فِي الْأَسَانِيدِ قَوْلٌ مُخْتَرَعٌ مُسْتَحْدَثٌ غَيْرُ مَسْبُوقٍ صَاحِبُهُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلَا مُسَاعِدَ لَهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ عَلَيْهِ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْقَوْلَ الشَّائِعَ الْمُتَّفَقَ عَلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ بِالْأَخْبَارِ وَالرِّوَايَاتِ قَدِيمًا وَحَدِيثًا أَنَّ كُلَّ رَجُلٍ ثِقَةٍ رَوَى عَنْ مِثْلِهِ حَدِيثًا وَجَائِزٌ مُمْكِنٌ لَهُ لِقَاؤُهُ وَالسَّمَاعُ مِنْهُ لِكَوْنِهِمَا جَمِيعًا كَانَا فِي عَصْرٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَأْتِ فِي خَبَرٍ قَطُّ أَنَّهُمَا اجْتَمَعَا وَلَا تَشَافَهَا بِكَلَامٍ، فَالرِّوَايَةُ ثَابِتَةٌ وَالْحُجَّةُ بِهَا لَازِمَةٌ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ هُنَاكَ دَلَالَةٌ بَيِّنَةٌ أَنَّ هَذَا الرَّاوِيَ لَمْ يَلْقَ مَنْ رَوَى عَنْهُ أَوْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "And this assertion—may God have mercy upon you—in criticizing chains of transmission is an invented, newly introduced doctrine, in which its proponent was preceded by no one, and in which he has no supporter among the people of knowledge. That is because the widespread, agreed-upon position among the scholars of reports and transmissions, both ancient and modern, is that whenever any trustworthy man transmits a hadith from someone like him, and it was possible and conceivable for him to have met him and heard from him because they both lived in the same era—whether or not no report has ever come down stating that they ever met or spoke face-to-face—the transmission is established and binding as proof, unless there exists clear evidence that this narrator never met the one from whom he transmitted or never heard anything from him."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Imām Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj, Muqaddimah Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1/30.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «ثَوْرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ الدِّيلِيُّ الْمَدَنِيُّ مَوْلَى بَنِي الدِّيلِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ. رَوَى عَنِ: الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ، وَسَالِمِ أَبِي الْغَيْثِ مَوْلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُطِيعٍ... وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَلَمْ يُدْرِكْهُ، وَعِكْرِمَةَ مَوْلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dīlī al-Madanī, freedman of Banū al-Dīl ibn Bakr. He transmitted from: al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Sālim Abū al-Ghayth the freedman of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṭīʿ ... and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās—though he did not reach his lifetime (wa-lam yudrikhu)—and ʿIkrimah the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Mizzī, Tahdhīb al-Kamāl fī Asmāʾ al-Rijāl 4/416–417, no. 860.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «قَالَ بِشْرُ بْنُ عُمَرَ الزَّهْرَانِيُّ: قُلْتُ لِمَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ: لَقِيَ ثَوْرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ؟ فَقَالَ: لَا، لَمْ يَلْقَهُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Bishr ibn ʿUmar al-Zahrānī said: I asked Mālik ibn Anas: 'Did Thawr ibn Zayd meet Ibn ʿAbbās?' He replied: 'No, he never met him.'"
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn al-ʿAlāʾī, Tuḥfat al-Taḥṣīl fī Dhikr Ruwāt al-Marāsīl 1/55, no. 116 (citing Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Marāsīl).

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «هَكَذَا هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ فِي الْمُوَطَّأِ عِنْدَ جَمَاعَةِ الرُّوَاةِ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ عَنْ ثَوْرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ لَيْسَ فِيهِ ذِكْرُ عِكْرِمَةَ، وَالْحَدِيثُ مَحْفُوظٌ لِعِكْرِمَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَإِنَّمَا رَوَاهُ ثَوْرٌ عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ... وَلَيْسَ فِي الْمُوَطَّأِ فِي هَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عِكْرِمَةُ، وَزَعَمُوا أَنَّ مَالِكًا أَسْقَطَ ذِكْرَ عِكْرِمَةَ مِنْهُ؛ لِأَنَّهُ كَرِهَ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي كِتَابِهِ لِكَلَامِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ وَغَيْرِهِ فِيهِ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Thus does this hadith appear in the Muwaṭṭaʾ among the generality of transmitters: 'from Mālik, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās,' with no mention of ʿIkrimah in it; whereas the hadith is preserved as belonging to ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Thawr only transmitted it from ʿIkrimah ... Yet ʿIkrimah is not in this isnād in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, and they maintained that Mālik dropped the mention of ʿIkrimah from it because he disliked having him in his book on account of the criticisms of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and others against him."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, al-Tamhīd li-mā fī al-Muwaṭṭaʾ min al-Maʿānī wa-l-Asānīd 2/26.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «وَقَالَ يَحْيَى بْنُ صَالِحٍ الْوُحَاظِيُّ: قُلْتُ لِابْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ: أَبُوكَ سَمِعَ مِنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ؟ قَالَ: مَنْ حَدَّثَكَ أَنَّ أَبِي سَمِعَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الصَّحَابَةِ غَيْرِ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ فَقَدْ كَذَبَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Wuḥāẓī said: I asked Ibn Abī Ḥāzim: 'Did your father hear from Abū Hurayrah?' He replied: 'Whoever told you that my father heard from any of the Companions other than Sahl ibn Saʿd has lied.'"
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Mizzī, Tahdhīb al-Kamāl 11/275, no. 2450; Shams al-Dīn al-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ 6/96–97.

arguments.header: How Did Hadith Critics Grade the Qurʾān's Reciters?
arguments.short_title: How Did Hadith Critics Grade the Qurʾān's Reciters?
arguments.reader_question: What did hadith critics write about the men who passed on the Qurʾān?
arguments.plain_english_hook: The transmitters who passed down the canonical Qurʾān recitations also appear in the biographical dictionaries of hadith critics. What did hadith critics write about the men who passed on the Qurʾān?
arguments.title: Biographical Evaluations of Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān and Canonical Qurʾān Reciters
arguments.executive_summary: Applying the biographical grading rules from the previous section to the transmitters of the Qurʾān, this section examines the rijāl notices on Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān—transmitter of the widely read Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim recitation—and other canonical Qurʾān reciters in the works of Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, Abū Ḥātim, Abū Zurʿah, Imām Muslim, al-Dhahabī, and Ibn Ḥajar, alongside Imām al-Ṭabarī's evaluations of specific variant readings in his Tafsīr. How did classical scholars separate a transmitter's standing in Qurʾān recitation from his grading in hadith?
arguments.methodological_significance: Comparing the assessments of canonical Qurʾān reciters in Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb, and Jāmiʿ al-Bayān illustrates how classical Sunni scholarship compartmentalized specialist mastery in recitation from precision in hadith narration. What does this compartmentalization reveal about how biographical grading rules functioned in practice?

subpoints.short_title: 4 Hadith Critics' Verdicts on Ḥafṣ, Whose Qurʾān Most Muslims Read
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see Ibn Maʿīn, al-Bukhārī, Muslim and al-Nasāʾī on Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān as a hadith narrator, reports that he copied books without hearing them, and how ʿadālah and ḍabṭ are defined.
subpoints.takeaway: Hadith critics graded Ḥafṣ “abandoned” in hadith; most printed Qurʾāns follow his transmission.
subpoints.title: Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān in Rijāl and the Separation of Qirāʾah from Ḥadīth

items.arabic: سألت يحيى بن معين عن حفص بن سليمان الأسدي فقال ليس بثقة
items.english: I asked Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn about Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān al-Asadī, and he said: 'He is not trustworthy.'

items.arabic: وقال البخاري تركوه وقال مسلم متروك
items.english: Al-Bukhārī said: 'They abandoned him.' And Muslim said: 'Abandoned [matrūk].'
A liar, abandoned, who fabricates hadith.

items.arabic: وقال النسائي ليس بثقة ولا يكتب حديثه
items.english: And al-Nasāʾī said: 'He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not to be written.'

subpoints.summary_markdown: The vast majority of contemporary printed editions of the Qurʾān follow the transmission of **Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān al-Asadī al-Kūfī** (90–180 AH) from his stepfather and teacher ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd (*Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim*), as recorded in the biographical registers of the Qurʾān reciters ([*Maʿrifat al-Qurrāʾ al-Kibār* 1/84](https://shamela.ws/book/8349/80); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/915)). Across the foundational Sunni *rijāl* encyclopedias, however, the early authorities of Hadith criticism evaluated Ḥafṣ as an unreliable transmitter, attributing his disqualification not merely to technical memory lapses, but to severe defects concerning textual integrity and moral probity ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173–174](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131); [*Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn* 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160); [*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/10–16](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558–559](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400–402](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916)).

evidence_items.label: Explicit Verdicts of Mendacity (Kadhdhāb) and Hadith Fabrication (Yaḍaʿu al-Ḥadīth)
evidence_items.content_markdown: **Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn** (d. 233 AH) contrasted Ḥafṣ's proficiency in Qurʾānic recitation with his status in Hadith transmission: *"Ḥafṣ was more proficient in recitation (aqraʾ) than Abū Bakr [ibn ʿAyyāsh], and he was a liar (kadhdhāb), whereas Abū Bakr was truthful (ṣadūq)"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/15](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)). **ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yūsuf ibn Khirāsh** (d. 283 AH) graded him *"a liar, abandoned, who fabricates Hadith (kadhdhāb matrūk yaḍaʿu al-ḥadīth)"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)), and **Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī** (d. 277 AH) stated: *"He is not to be believed (lā yuṣaddaq), abandoned in Hadith (matrūk al-ḥadīth)"* ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173–174](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1132)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «كذاب متروك يضع الحديث» — "A liar, abandoned, who fabricates hadith." ([Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916))

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: كذاب متروك يضع الحديث
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: A liar, abandoned, who fabricates hadith.

evidence_items.label: Reports of Copying Manuscripts Without Audition (Min Ghayr Samāʿ) and Inverting Chains (Qalb al-Asānīd)
evidence_items.content_markdown: **Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj** (d. 160 AH), as transmitted by **Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān** (d. 198 AH), provided a direct contemporary testimony: *"Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān took a book from me and did not return it; and he used to take people's books and copy them"* ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916)). **Ibn Ḥibbān** (d. 354 AH) similarly documented the specific grounds for his critical evaluation: *"He used to invert chains of transmission (yaqlibu al-asānīd), elevate disconnected reports (yarfaʿu al-marāsīl), and take people's books, copy them, and transmit them without audition (min ghayr samāʿ)"* ([*Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn* 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «كان يقلب الأسانيد ويرفع المراسيل وكان يأخذ كتب الناس فينسخها ويرويها من غير سماع» — "He would invert chains, elevate mursal reports, and take people's books to copy and narrate them without hearing them." ([Al-Majrūḥīn 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160))

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: كان يقلب الأسانيد ويرفع المراسيل وكان يأخذ كتب الناس فينسخها ويرويها من غير سماع
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: He would invert chains, elevate mursal reports, and take people's books to copy and narrate them without hearing them.

evidence_items.label: Prohibition of Transmission and Exclusion by the Compilers of the Ṣaḥīḥayn and Early Hadith Critics
evidence_items.content_markdown: **ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī** (d. 198 AH) stated under oath: *"By God, it is not permissible (mā taḥillu) to transmit from him"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916)), while **ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī** (d. 234 AH) declared: *"I abandoned him deliberately (taraktuhu ʿalā ʿamd)"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/14](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/)). Both **al-Bukhārī** (d. 256 AH) and **Muslim** (d. 261 AH) excluded his narrations from the *Ṣaḥīḥayn*, with al-Bukhārī recording that *"they abandoned him (tarakūhu)"* and Muslim, **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** (d. 241 AH), and **al-Nasāʾī** (d. 303 AH) grading him *"abandoned in Hadith (matrūk al-ḥadīth)"* ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400–401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/915); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «وقال البخاري تركوه وقال مسلم متروك وقال النسائي ليس بثقة ولا يكتب حديثه» — "Al-Bukhārī said: 'They abandoned him.' Muslim said: 'Abandoned (matrūk).' Al-Nasāʾī said: 'He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not to be written.'" ([Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916))

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: وقال البخاري تركوه وقال مسلم متروك وقال النسائي ليس بثقة ولا يكتب حديثه
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: Al-Bukhārī said: 'They abandoned him.' Muslim said: 'Abandoned (matrūk).' Al-Nasāʾī said: 'He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not to be written.'

evidence_items.label: The Epistemological Specialization: Treating Qurʾānic Transmission and Prophetic Reports as Distinct Domains
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ* (1/104)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/) and **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī's** *Nuzhat al-Naẓar* ([IslamWeb Fatwa #232843](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/232843/)), narrator criticism (*al-ṭaʿn*) is divided into five domain-specific memory defects (*ḍabṭ*) and five global moral defects (*ʿadālah*), headed by lying (*kadhib*, which yields a fabricated [*mawḍūʿ*] report) and accusation of lying (*tuhmatuhu bi-l-kadhib*, which yields an abandoned [*matrūk*] narrator). Because **Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān** was explicitly criticized in the primary *rijāl* compendia for lying (*kadhdhāb*) and fabricating Hadith (*yaḍaʿu al-ḥadīth*) ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/15](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)), inverting chains (*yaqlibu al-asānīd*) and narrating copied manuscripts without audition (*min ghayr samāʿ*) ([*Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn* 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160)), and graded *matrūk al-ḥadīth* ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173–174](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1132)), his disqualification falls under the category of moral probity (*ʿadālah*), which in classical legal and hadith theory governs the admissibility of testimony across all religious sciences ([*Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ* 1/104](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «ثم الطعن إما أن يكون لكذب الراوي أو تهمته بذلك» — "Then criticism is either due to the narrator's lying, or accusation thereof." ([Ibn Ḥajar, Nuzhat al-Naẓar](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/232843/))

«أَخَذَ مِنِّي حَفْصُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ كِتَابًا فَلَمْ يَرُدَّهُ، وَكَانَ يَأْخُذُ كُتُبَ النَّاسِ فَيَنْسَخُهَا»
Ḥafṣ took a book from me and did not return it; he used to take people's books and copy them
Weak in Hadith, and I abandoned him deliberately
«لَا يُكْتَبُ حَدِيثُهُ... لَا يُصَدَّقُ، مَتْرُوكُ الْحَدِيثِ»
His Hadith is not to be written; he is not to be believed (*lā yuṣaddaq*), abandoned
A liar (*kadhdhāb*), abandoned; he fabricates Hadith (*yaḍaʿu al-ḥadīth*)
«لَيْسَ بِثِقَةٍ، وَلَا يُكْتَبُ حَدِيثُهُ... مَتْرُوكُ الْحَدِيثِ»
Not trustworthy, his Hadith is not written; abandoned in Hadith
«كَانَ يَقْلِبُ الْأَسَانِيدَ، وَيَرْفَعُ الْمَرَاسِيلَ، وَكَانَ يَأْخُذُ كُتُبَ النَّاسِ فَيَنْسَخُهَا وَيَرْوِيهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ سَمَاعٍ»
He used to invert chains, elevate mursal reports, and copy people's books and transmit them without audition

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Traditional commentators and biographers cite secondary reports in which Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal described Ḥafṣ as 'acceptable (ṣāliḥ)' or 'having no harm in him (mā bihi baʾs)' ([*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/915); [*Maʿrifat al-Qurrāʾ al-Kibār* 1/84](https://shamela.ws/book/8349/80)), alongside al-Dhahabī's observation that he was 'reliable and precise in recitation, unlike his state in Hadith' ([*Maʿrifat al-Qurrāʾ al-Kibār* 1/84](https://shamela.ws/book/8349/80); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)), arguing that severe criticisms against him pertained strictly to his retention of Hadith rather than his integrity.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In the primary *rijāl* record, both Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal's son ʿAbd Allāh and Ḥanbal ibn Isḥāq also transmitted Aḥmad's stricter evaluation grading Ḥafṣ *'abandoned in Hadith (matrūk al-ḥadīth)'* ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/915)). Furthermore, under the classical methodological principles of *uṣūl al-ḥadīth*, detailed disparagement (*al-jarḥ al-mufassar*)—such as Shuʿbah's first-hand testimony regarding unreturned and copied manuscripts ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131)) and Ibn Ḥibbān's specification of chain inversion (*qalb al-asānīd*) and transmitting copied books without audition ([*Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn* 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160))—takes precedence over general expressions of approval (*al-taʿdīl al-mujmal*). In the primary biographical record, however, **Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn** explicitly contrasted Ḥafṣ's mendacity (*kadhdhāb*) with the truthfulness (*ṣadūq*) of his co-student **Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh** within the exact sentence comparing their mastery of ʿĀṣim's recitation ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/15](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916)), while **Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj** and **Ibn Ḥibbān** described specific actions—retaining borrowed manuscripts, copying books to transmit them without audition (*min ghayr samāʿ*), and inverting chains (*qalb al-asānīd*) ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1131); [*Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn* 1/255](https://shamela.ws/book/5834/160)). Furthermore, the formal taxonomy of **Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ** ([*Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ* 1/104](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/)) and **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** ([IslamWeb Fatwa #232843](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/232843/)) classifies *kadhib* and *tuhmatuhu bi-l-kadhib* (*matrūk*) under moral defects of probity (*ʿadālah*), explicitly distinguishing them from technical memory weakness (*sūʾ al-ḥifẓ* or *kathrat al-ghalaṭ*).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
#### 1. Grading Ḥafṣ in Classical Rijāl Criticism

When **Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn** ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 7/15](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/1479/); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)) evaluated ʿĀṣim's primary transmitters, he separated Qurʾānic recitation from Hadith transmission, grading Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh truthful while classifying Ḥafṣ under mendacity (*kadhdhāb*). **Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī** ([*al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl* 3/173–174](https://shamela.ws/book/2170/1132)) ruled that Ḥafṣ's prophetic traditions must neither be transcribed nor credited, and secondary reports from **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** formally transmitted his abandonment ([*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/400](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/915)). This matches the total exclusion of Ḥafṣ's chains from the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* of **al-Bukhārī** and **Muslim**, alongside severe gradings by **Ibn Khirāsh** and **al-Nasāʾī** ([*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 2/401](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/916)). This difference between biographical narrator criticism and scriptural reception remains a foundational tension in the classical sciences.

#### 2. Taxonomic Conflict in Specialization

To harmonize Ḥafṣ's canonical standing in Qurʾānic recitation with his disparagement in Hadith registers, scholars formulated a compartmentalized defense. **Shams al-Dīn al-Dhahabī** ([*Maʿrifat al-Qurrāʾ al-Kibār* 1/84–85](https://shamela.ws/book/8349/80); [*Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl* 1/558–559](https://shamela.ws/book/1692/558)) proposed that Ḥafṣ mastered ʿĀṣim's reading but was weak in Hadith retention, comparing him inversely to al-Aʿmash. **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** compressed this distinction in *Taqrīb al-Tahdhīb* (cf. [*Tuḥfat al-Aḥwadhī* 8/175](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/56/5594/)).

However, this compartmentalization encounters structural difficulties within Hadith theory. In [*Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ* (Type 23)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/90/54/), probative transmission requires both moral integrity (*ʿadālah*) and technical retention (*ḍabṭ*). In [*Nuzhat al-Naẓar* (pp. 74–113)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/fatwa/232843/), **Ibn Ḥajar** separates memory flaws from character flaws like lying. Because early critics impugned Ḥafṣ with character-level charges (*matrūk*, *kadhdhāb*) rather than mere forgetfulness, his grading falls under the indivisible category of *ʿadālah*, which governs testimony across all religious disciplines.

#### 3. Single-Strand (*Āḥād*) Stemmata in Qirāʾāt

Individual biographical scrutiny cannot be bypassed by asserting mass concurrent transmission (*tawātur*). **Ibn al-Jazarī** ([*al-Nashr fī al-Qirāʾāt al-ʿAshr* 1/13](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/70/5/); [1/156](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/70/30/)) conceded that requiring mass concurrency for every variant word would invalidate numerous authenticated canonical readings, which rely instead on chain soundness. Furthermore, **Shady Hekmat Nasser** (2012; 2020) notes by mapping stemmata that each canonical reading passes through single-strand (*āḥād*) bottlenecks at the tier of the Eponymous Reader and his primary transmitters, while **Marijn van Putten** (2022) observes occasional consonantal departures from the ʿUthmānic skeleton. Applying either discipline's epistemological standard consistently challenges the foundational premises of the other.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «كَانَ حَفْصُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ عَيَّاشٍ مِنْ أَعْلَمِ النَّاسِ بِقِرَاءَةِ عَاصِمٍ، وَكَانَ حَفْصٌ أَقْرَأَ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَكَانَ كَذَّابًا، وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ صَدُوقًا»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh were among the most knowledgeable of people regarding the recitation of ʿĀṣim; Ḥafṣ was more proficient in recitation (aqraʾ) than Abū Bakr, and he was a liar (kadhdhāb), whereas Abū Bakr was truthful (ṣadūq)."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn (via Zakariyyā al-Sājī), in al-Mizzī, Tahdhīb al-Kamāl 7/15; Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401; cf. al-Dhahabī, Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl 1/558.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «وَاللَّهِ مَا تَحِلُّ الرِّوَايَةُ عَنْهُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "By God, it is not permissible (mā taḥillu) to transmit from him."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, in Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «أَخَذَ مِنِّي حَفْصُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ كِتَابًا فَلَمْ يَرُدَّهُ، وَكَانَ يَأْخُذُ كُتُبَ النَّاسِ فَيَنْسَخُهَا»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān took a book from me and did not return it; and he used to take people's books and copy them."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Shuʿbah ibn al-Ḥajjāj (via Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān), in Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 3/173; Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «ضَعِيفُ الْحَدِيثِ، وَتَرَكْتُهُ عَلَى عَمْدٍ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "He is weak in Hadith (ḍaʿīf al-ḥadīth), and I abandoned him deliberately (wa-taraktuhu ʿalā ʿamd)."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, in al-Mizzī, Tahdhīb al-Kamāl 7/14; Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «كَانَ يَقْلِبُ الْأَسَانِيدَ، وَيَرْفَعُ الْمَرَاسِيلَ، وَكَانَ يَأْخُذُ كُتُبَ النَّاسِ فَيَنْسَخُهَا وَيَرْوِيهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ سَمَاعٍ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "He used to invert chains of transmission (yaqlibu al-asānīd) and elevate disconnected reports into prophetic traditions (yarfaʿu al-marāsīl), and he used to take people's books, copy them, and transmit them without having heard them (min ghayr samāʿ)."
arabic_blockquotes.citation: Ibn Ḥibbān al-Bustī, Kitāb al-Majrūḥīn 1/255; quoted in al-Dhahabī, Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl 1/558 and Ibn Ḥajar, Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb 2/401.

subpoints.summary_markdown: The methodological tension between canonical Qurʾānic transmission and *ʿilm al-rijāl* (narrator criticism) extends beyond Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān across the wider network of canonical Readers (*qurrāʾ*) and primary transmitters (*ruwāt*) ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 13/476–478](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/3252/); [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* 8/497–502](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/1431/)). Classical biographical dictionaries ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 30/248–250](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/7879/); [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* 10/327](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/1754/)) and early exegetes such as **Imām al-Ṭabarī** (d. 310 AH) ([*Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 12/137–138](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/50/1901/); [*Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 1/542](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/50/138/)) record substantive critiques regarding the memory, precision, and grammatical choices of several figures whose readings were subsequently canonized.

evidence_items.label: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār (d. 245 AH — Canonical Rāwī of Ibn ʿĀmir & Narrator in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī): Charging Fees per Sheet and Accepting Prompted Narrations (Talqīn)
evidence_items.content_markdown: **Hishām ibn ʿAmmār** (d. 245 AH)—both the canonical Damascus transmitter (*rāwī*) of **Ibn ʿĀmir** and a narrator cited in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī*—was described as *"flighty and light (ṭayyāsh khafīf)"* by **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal**, charged fees of one dirham per two sheets to narrate hadith according to **Ṣāliḥ Jazarah**, **Ibn Wārah**, and **Ibn Sayyār**, and accepted material prompted to him (*talqīn*) later in life according to **Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī** ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 30/248–250](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/7879/); [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* 11/424–425](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/2059/)). Furthermore, **Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī** stated: *"Hishām narrated over 400 baseless hadiths (laysa lahā aṣl) with complete chains... prompted to him by Faḍlak; Hishām ibn ʿAmmār said: 'Narrate to me; it has already been transmitted, so I do not care who bears the error'... and I [Abū Dāwūd] feared he would cause a rupture in Islam"* ([*Tahdhīb al-Kamāl* 30/248–249](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1001/7879/); [*Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ* 11/424–425](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/60/2059/); [*Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb* 11/53–54](https://shamela.ws/book/3310/4836)).

evidence_items.label: Imām al-Ṭabarī's (d. 310 AH) Pre-Canonization Critiques of Canonical Readings Regarding Arabic Grammar and Transmitter Fallibility
evidence_items.content_markdown: Writing shortly before **Ibn Mujāhid's** (d. 324 AH) formal canonization of the Seven Readings, **Imām al-Ṭabarī** (d. 310 AH) evaluated and rejected several variant readings that were later classified as *mutawātir*: he criticized **Ibn ʿĀmir's** reading at [Qurʾān 6:137](https://quran.com/6/137) as *"unpleasant and uneloquent in Arabic speech (qabīḥ ghayr faṣīḥ)"* and *"linguistically invalid (fasād)"* ([*Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 12/137–138](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/50/1901/)), and characterized **Ḥamzah's** reading at [Qurʾān 4:1](https://quran.com/4/1) as *"inferior in grammatical inflection (al-radīʾ fī al-iʿrāb)"* ([*Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 7/520–523](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/50/1161/)). Similarly, at [Qurʾān 2:37](https://quran.com/2/37), al-Ṭabarī set aside **Ibn Kathīr's** canonical reading on the grounds that it rested on the report of *"one who is subject to forgetfulness and error (man yajūzu ʿalayhi al-sahw wa-l-khaṭaʾ)"* ([*Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 1/542](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/50/138/)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «وَكَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلَٰدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ لِيُرْدُوهُمْ وَلِيَلْبِسُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ دِينَهُمْ» — "And likewise, to many of the polytheists their partners have made pleasing the killing of their children in order to bring about their destruction and to cover them with confusion in their religion." ([Qurʾān 6:137 (cf. Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī 12/137–138)](https://quran.com/6/137))
