subpoints.summary_markdown: Commentators often connect these traditions to the 1453 AD Ottoman conquest of Constantinople and the 1258 AD Mongol sack of Baghdad, while the primary texts themselves describe a weaponless capture immediately before the *Dajjāl* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2897](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2897), [2920a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2920a)), an eighth-century mobilization for Maslamah's 717 AD siege ([*Musnad Aḥmad* 18957](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18191/)), and low-lying land named al-Baṣrah ([*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4306](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4306)).

evidence_items.label: Sequence of Events in the Malāḥim Reports (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2897, 2900 & 2920a; Bukhārī 2924) and the Maslamah Clause (Musnad Aḥmad 18957)
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2897](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2897), [2900](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2900), and [2920a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2920a) (cf. [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4294](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4294)), Constantinople is conquered only after a Syrian apocalyptic battle at al-Aʿmāq or Dābiq and Medina's ruin (`خَرَابُ يَثْرِبَ`), falls **without weapons or arrows** (`فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوا بِسِلَاحٍ وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا بِسَهْمٍ`) when its walls fall at the vocal chant of *takbīr*, and is followed immediately—while the conquerors' swords hang on olive trees (`قَدْ عَلَّقُوا سُيُوفَهُمْ بِالزَّيْتُونِ`)—by the emergence of the *Dajjāl* (`لاَ نَرَى الدَّجَّالَ يَخْرُجُ حَتَّى تُفْتَحَ الرُّومُ`) and the descent of Jesus. Meanwhile, whereas [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2924](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2924) merely promises forgiveness to the first army raiding Caesar's City (`أَوَّلُ جَيْشٍ مِنْ أُمَّتِي يَغْزُونَ مَدِينَةَ قَيْصَرَ مَغْفُورٌ لَهُمْ`), the separate praise report in [*Musnad Aḥmad* #18478 (ed. #18957)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18191/), [*al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr* 1216](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/84/1207/), [*al-Mustadrak* 8300](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/74/8181/), and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's [*al-Istīʿāb* 1/170 (#186)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1080/210/) passes through a single narrow stem (`al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah ← ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr ← his father Bishr`, from whom no one narrated except his son: `وَلَمْ يَرْوِ عَنْهُ غَيْرُ ابْنِهِ`) and concludes with Bishr's statement that he narrated it to **Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik**, who thereupon launched his unsuccessful 717–718 AD (98–99 AH) siege.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ الرُّومُ بِالأَعْمَاقِ أَوْ بِدَابِقٍ فَيَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمْ جَيْشٌ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ» — "The Hour will not be established until the Romans camp at al-Aʿmāq or at Dābiq, and an army from the city will go out to face them." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2897; cf. Musnad Aḥmad 18957)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ الرُّومُ بِالأَعْمَاقِ أَوْ بِدَابِقٍ فَيَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمْ جَيْشٌ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: The Hour will not be established until the Romans camp at al-Aʿmāq or at Dābiq, and an army from the city will go out to face them.

evidence_items.label: Weaponless End-Times Capture (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2920a; Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 2928 & 3592) Alongside the Basra (Banū Qanṭūrāʾ) Bottleneck at Saʿīd ibn Jumhān (d. 136 AH)
evidence_items.content_markdown: Whereas [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2920a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2920a) depicts seventy thousand descendants of Isaac capturing Constantinople without weapons or arrows (`فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوا بِسِلاَحٍ وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا بِسَهْمٍ`) immediately before the *Dajjāl* emerges, and [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2928](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2928) and [3592](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3592) (cf. [3593](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3593)) describe end-times fighting against the Turks (`التُّرْكَ صِغَارَ الأَعْيُنِ`) without naming Baghdad, the *Banū Qanṭūrāʾ* tradition in [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4306](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4306) and [*Musnad Aḥmad* #19900 (ed. #20413)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/19520/) and [#19938 (ed. #20451)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/19555/) explicitly names **al-Baṣrah** (`يُسَمُّونَهُ الْبَصْرَةَ`), promises victory to its defenders (**«وَيَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ عَلَى بَقِيَّتِهَا»**, *"and God will grant victory to its remnant"*), and appears in its earliest second-century sources ([*Muṣannaf ʿAbd al-Razzāq* 20799](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/73/19840/); [*Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah* #296 (ed. #38400)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/10/5587/)) as a non-prophetic (*mawqūf*) statement of **ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr** citing *"the Book"* (`فَهَكَذَا نَجِدُهُ فِي الْكِتَابِ`, cf. Genesis 25:1–4, Keturah). Every Prophetic (*marfūʿ*) version bottlenecks exclusively at the solitary Basran narrator **Saʿīd ibn Jumhān (d. 136 AH / 753 AD)**—who died nine years before Baghdad was founded (145 AH / 762 AD), fluctuated across three different sons of Abū Bakrah in his *isnād*, and whose father was killed by the Khārijite Azāriqah (`قَتَلَتْهُ الْأَزَارِقَةُ`; [*Musnad Aḥmad* 18923](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18602/); [*al-Mustadrak* 6435 / 6494](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/74/6323/)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: «لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَغْزُوَهَا سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْحَاقَ فَإِذَا جَاءُوهَا نَزَلُوا فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوا بِسِلاَحٍ وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا بِسَهْمٍ» — "The Hour will not be established until seventy thousand descendants of Isaac raid it; when they come to it and alight, they will neither fight with a weapon nor shoot an arrow." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2920a; cf. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4306)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَغْزُوَهَا سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْحَاقَ فَإِذَا جَاءُوهَا نَزَلُوا فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوا بِسِلاَحٍ وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا بِسَهْمٍ
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: The Hour will not be established until seventy thousand descendants of Isaac raid it; when they come to it and alight, they will neither fight with a weapon nor shoot an arrow.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Traditional commentators and modern harmonizers frequently propose that Musnad Aḥmad 18957 foretold Sultan Mehmed II's 1453 AD conquest of Constantinople while Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2897/2920a refers to a separate end-times conquest, and suggest that 'al-Baṣrah' in Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4306 may be understood broadly to encompass the 1258 AD Mongol siege of Baghdad.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: [*Musnad Aḥmad* 18957](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18191/) is a single-strand report transmitted through the obscure narrator Bishr al-Khathʿamī ([*al-Istīʿāb* 1/170 (#186)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1080/210/)) whose text explicitly notes that it was cited to mobilize Umayyad Prince Maslamah's 717–718 AD campaign (`فَحَدَّثْتُهُ فَغَزَا الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ`), whereas the canonical traditions ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2897](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2897), [2900](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2900), [2920a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2920a); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2924](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2924); [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4294](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4294)) either promise forgiveness to the first Umayyad army raiding Caesar's City or place Constantinople's capture after Medina's ruin, achieved without weapons through *takbīr* immediately prior to the emergence of the *Dajjāl*. Similarly, while [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2928](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2928) and [3592](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3592) (cf. [3593](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3593)) mention fighting the Turks in general terms, [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4306](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4306) and [*Musnad Aḥmad* 20413](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/19520/) explicitly specify **al-Baṣrah** (`يُسَمُّونَهُ الْبَصْرَةَ`), promise victory to its surviving inhabitants (`وَيَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ عَلَى بَقِيَّتِهَا`—in contrast to the destruction of Baghdad in 1258 AD), and trace through the pre-Baghdad Basran narrator Saʿīd ibn Jumhān (d. 136 AH) to a non-prophetic scriptural statement of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ([*Muṣannaf ʿAbd al-Razzāq* 20799](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/73/19840/); [*Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah* 38400](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/10/5587/)).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Eighth-Century Basran Controls on the *Banū Qanṭūrāʾ* Tradition (*Abū Dāwūd* 4306)
Modern harmonizations frequently interpret the *Banū Qanṭūrāʾ* report in [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4306](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4306) as a prophecy of the 1258 AD (656 AH) Mongol destruction of Baghdad. While [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2928](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2928) and [3592](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3592) (followed by [3593](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3593) on end-times warfare) contain general traditions about fighting the Turks (*al-Turk ṣighār al-aʿyun*), three primary-source controls anchor the *Banū Qanṭūrāʾ* tradition firmly in early eighth-century Basra:
* **Explicit Naming of al-Baṣrah and Victory Outcome:** The Arabic *matn* specifies low-lying ground named **al-Baṣrah** (*yusammūnahu al-Baṣrah*) beside the lower Tigris (*Dijlat al-ʿAwrāʾ*) crossed by Basra's famous pontoon bridge (*Jisr al-Baṣrah*). Moreover, the fuller recensions in *Musnad Aḥmad* ([20413](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/19520/) and [20451](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/19555/)) conclude with God granting military triumph to the city's steadfast remnant (*wa-yaftaḥu Llāhu ʿalā baqiyyatihā*)—the exact opposite of the 1258 AD annihilation of Baghdad.
* **Pre-Canonical *Mawqūf* Stratum:** In *Muṣannaf ʿAbd al-Razzāq* ([20799](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/73/19840/)), the earliest recorded form of the warning is an unattributed (*mawqūf*) remark from **ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr**, who in *Muṣannaf Ibn Abī Shaybah* ([38400](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/10/5587/)) states that he derived the apocalyptic ethnonyms *Banū Qanṭūrāʾ* (descendants of Abraham's wife Keturah in Genesis 25:1–4) from earlier written scripture (`فِي الْكِتَابِ`).
* **The Pre-Baghdad Bottleneck `Saʿīd ibn Jumhān` (d. 136 AH):** Every Prophetic chain passes exclusively through the Basran transmitter **Saʿīd ibn Jumhān**, who died nine years before Caliph al-Manṣūr founded Baghdad (145 AH / 762 AD), vacillated (*iḍṭirāb*) among three separate sons of Abū Bakrah in his chains, and stated that his own father Jumhān was slain by the Khārijite Azāriqah (*qatalathu al-Azāriqah*; *al-Mustadrak* [6435 / 6494](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/74/6323/) and *Musnad Aḥmad* [18923](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18602/)).

### 2. Umayyad Siege Mobilization in *Musnad Aḥmad* 18957 vs. Canonical Apocalypse
A similar historical seam governs the popular saying praising the commander and army that conquer Constantinople. Excluded from all Six Canonical Books—where [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2924](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2924) instead promises forgiveness to the *first* army raiding Caesar's City (`مَدِينَةَ قَيْصَرَ`)—this report survives via a solitary Egyptian family chain (transmitted by al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bishr, from his father Bishr al-Khathʿamī, from whom only his son narrated) recorded in *Musnad Aḥmad* ([report 18957](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/6/18191/)), al-Ṭabarānī's *al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr* ([no. 1216](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/84/1207/)), al-Ḥākim's *Mustadrak* ([#8300](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/74/8181/)), along with the biographical entry in *al-Istīʿāb* ([1/170](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1080/210/)). Crucially, the narration appends an explicit historical frame: Umayyad prince **Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik** summoned Bishr, heard this report, and immediately launched his 98–99 AH (717–718 AD) siege of Constantinople (*fa-ghazā al-Qusṭanṭīniyyah*). Conversely, the canonical Constantinople traditions ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2897](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2897), [2900](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2900), and [2920a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2920a); [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 4294](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4294)) describe an end-times miracle after Medina's desolation (`خَرَابُ يَثْرِبَ`), where the walls fall at *Lā ilāha illā Allāh wa-Allāhu Akbar* without weapons or arrows, followed immediately by the *Dajjāl*.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ الرُّومُ بِالأَعْمَاقِ أَوْ بِدَابِقٍ فَيَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمْ جَيْشٌ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ مِنْ خِيَارِ أَهْلِ الأَرْضِ يَوْمَئِذٍ... فَيَفْتَتِحُونَ قُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَقْتَسِمُونَ الْغَنَائِمَ قَدْ عَلَّقُوا سُيُوفَهُمْ بِالزَّيْتُونِ إِذْ صَاحَ فِيهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِنَّ الْمَسِيحَ قَدْ خَلَفَكُمْ فِي أَهْلِيكُمْ فَيَخْرُجُونَ وَذَلِكَ بَاطِلٌ فَإِذَا جَاءُوا الشَّأْمَ خَرَجَ فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يُعِدُّونَ لِلْقِتَالِ يُسَوُّونَ الصُّفُوفَ إِذْ أُقِيمَتِ الصَّلاَةُ فَيَنْزِلُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "The Hour will not be established until the Romans camp at al-Aʿmāq or at Dābiq, and an army from the city will go out to face them, from the best people on earth at that time... Then they will conquer Constantinople. While they are dividing the spoils, having hung their swords on olive trees, Satan will cry out among them that the False Messiah [Dajjāl] has taken their place among their families. They will go out—though that report is false—and when they reach Syria, he [the Dajjāl] will emerge; and while they are preparing for battle and straightening the ranks, the prayer will be called and Jesus son of Mary will descend."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «تَغْزُونَ جَزِيرَةَ الْعَرَبِ فَيَفْتَحُهَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ فَارِسَ فَيَفْتَحُهَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ تَغْزُونَ الرُّومَ فَيَفْتَحُهَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ تَغْزُونَ الدَّجَّالَ فَيَفْتَحُهُ اللَّهُ. قَالَ فَقَالَ نَافِعٌ يَا جَابِرُ لاَ نَرَى الدَّجَّالَ يَخْرُجُ حَتَّى تُفْتَحَ الرُّومُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "You will attack the Arabian Peninsula and God will enable you to conquer it, then Persia and God will enable you to conquer it, then you will attack Rome and God will enable you to conquer it, then you will attack the Dajjāl and God will enable you to conquer him." Nāfiʿ [ibn ʿUtbah] said: "O Jābir, we do not see the Dajjāl emerging until Rome is conquered."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يَغْزُوَهَا سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْحَاقَ فَإِذَا جَاءُوهَا نَزَلُوا فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوا بِسِلاَحٍ وَلَمْ يَرْمُوا بِسَهْمٍ قَالُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَيَسْقُطُ أَحَدُ جَانِبَيْهَا... فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَقْتَسِمُونَ الْغَنَائِمَ إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الصَّرِيخُ فَقَالَ إِنَّ الدَّجَّالَ قَدْ خَرَجَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "The Hour will not be established until seventy thousand descendants of Isaac raid it [Constantinople]; when they come to it and alight, they will neither fight with a weapon nor shoot an arrow. They will say: 'There is no god but God, and God is Greatest,' and one of its sides will fall... And while they are dividing the spoils, a crier will come to them and say: 'Indeed, the Dajjāl has emerged!'"

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «أَوَّلُ جَيْشٍ مِنْ أُمَّتِي يَغْزُونَ مَدِينَةَ قَيْصَرَ مَغْفُورٌ لَهُمْ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "The first army from my community that raids Caesar's City [Constantinople] will be forgiven."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى تُقَاتِلُوا التُّرْكَ صِغَارَ الأَعْيُنِ، حُمْرَ الْوُجُوهِ، ذُلْفَ الأُنُوفِ، كَأَنَّ وُجُوهَهُمُ الْمَجَانُّ الْمُطَرَّقَةُ، وَلاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى تُقَاتِلُوا قَوْمًا نِعَالُهُمُ الشَّعَرُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "The Hour will not be established until you fight the Turks—people with small eyes, red faces, and flat noses, their faces like shields coated with leather—and the Hour will not be established until you fight a people whose sandals are hair."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «يَنْزِلُ نَاسٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي بِغَائِطٍ يُسَمُّونَهُ الْبَصْرَةَ عِنْدَ نَهْرٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ دِجْلَةُ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ جِسْرٌ... فَإِذَا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ جَاءَ بَنُو قَنْطُورَاءَ عِرَاضُ الْوُجُوهِ صِغَارُ الْأَعْيُنِ حَتَّى يَنْزِلُوا عَلَى شَطِّ النَّهْرِ، فَيَتَفَرَّقُ أَهْلُهَا ثَلَاثَ فِرَقٍ: فِرْقَةٌ يَأْخُذُونَ أَذْنَابَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْبَرِّيَّةَ وَهَلَكُوا، وَفِرْقَةٌ يَأْخُذُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَكَفَرُوا، وَفِرْقَةٌ يَجْعَلُونَ ذَرَارِيَّهُمْ خَلْفَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَيُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ وَهُمُ الشُّهَدَاءُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Some of my people will alight on low-lying ground, which they will call al-Baṣrah, beside a river called the Tigris over which there is a bridge... At the end of time the Banū Qanṭūrāʾ will come with broad faces and small eyes and alight on the bank of the river. The town's inhabitants will then separate into three sections: one section will follow cattle and live in the desert and perish; another will seek security for themselves and disbelieve; but a third will put their children behind their backs and fight them, and they will be the martyrs."

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «لَتُفْتَحَنَّ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةُ، فَلَنِعْمَ الْأَمِيرُ أَمِيرُهَا، وَلَنِعْمَ الْجَيْشُ ذَلِكَ الْجَيْشُ. قَالَ: فَدَعَانِي مَسْلَمَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ فَسَأَلَنِي، فَحَدَّثْتُهُ، فَغَزَا الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: "Constantinople will certainly be conquered; what an excellent commander its commander will be, and what an excellent army that army will be." He [the narrator, Bishr al-Khathʿamī / al-Ghanawī] said: "So Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik summoned me and asked me, so I narrated it to him, and thereupon he campaigned against Constantinople!"

arguments.header: Do Ṣaḥīḥ Reports of the Same Event Agree?
arguments.short_title: Do Ṣaḥīḥ Reports of the Same Event Agree?
arguments.reader_question: When reports of one event differ, how did classical commentators explain it?
arguments.plain_english_hook: On several public events and biographical milestones—from the Meccan stay and the eclipse prayer to the Farewell Hajj—Bukhārī and Muslim preserve multiple accounts. How did commentators explain them?
arguments.title: Chronological Figures, Public Events, and Classical Reconciliation Methods
arguments.executive_summary: This concluding section examines six cases where authenticated chains in Bukhārī and Muslim record different timelines or descriptions of major public events: ages 60, 63, and 65 for the Prophet's life (with 7 + 8 = 15 in Muslim 2353e), 4, 6, or 8 bowings in the solar eclipse prayer on the day Ibrāhīm died, the mode of the Farewell Hajj and whether he prayed inside the Kaʿbah, the first and last Qurʾānic revelations, the prohibition of temporary marriage (mutʿah), and the Farewell Sermon bequest. How do the classical reconciliations compare with the wording of each report?
arguments.methodological_significance: In their commentaries, scholars such as al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, al-Bukhārī, al-Nawawī, Ibn Taymiyyah, and Ibn Ḥajar sometimes proposed reconciliation (jamʿ) and in other cases preferred one chain (tarjīḥ) and attributed the alternative figures to narrator oversight (wahm). What criteria determine when a differing ṣaḥīḥ report can be harmonized and when one report is set aside?

subpoints.takeaway: Ṣaḥīḥ reports give ages 60, 63 and 65; Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī attributed some to narrator error (wahm).

items.who: 10 yrs in Mecca · Ibn ʿAbbās / Anas
13 yrs in Mecca · Ibn ʿAbbās / ʿĀʾishah

subpoints.summary_markdown: Within *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās** and **Anas ibn Mālik** report three different figures for the Prophet's stay in Mecca and age at death: **10 years** and age **60** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5900](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5900); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2347a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2347a)), **13 years** and age **63** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3902](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3902); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2351a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2351a)), and **15 years** (`7 + 8`) and age **65** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353a)–[2353e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353e)). Classical commentators such as **al-Nawawī** and **Ibn Ḥajar** discussed both rounding explanations and narrator oversight (*wahm*).

evidence_items.label: 10 Years in Mecca & Death at Age 60 via Anas ibn Mālik, ʿĀʾishah, and Ibn ʿAbbās
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5900](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5900) (cf. 3547–3548) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2347a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2347a)–[2347b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2347b), Anas ibn Mālik reports that the Prophet resided in Mecca for 10 years and died at age 60. Parallel reports supporting the 10-year / age 60 count are also recorded from ʿĀʾishah ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2350a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2350a)) and Ibn ʿAbbās ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4464](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4464)–[4465](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4465), [4978](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4978)–[4979](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4979)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: بِمَكَّةَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ يُنْزَلُ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ وَبِالْمَدِينَةِ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ (He stayed in Mecca ten years while the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and in Medina ten years — Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4978)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: بِمَكَّةَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ يُنْزَلُ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ وَبِالْمَدِينَةِ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: He stayed in Mecca ten years while the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and in Medina ten years

evidence_items.label: 13 Years in Mecca & Death at Age 63 via the Same Companion (Ibn ʿAbbās) and a Divergent Core Chain
evidence_items.content_markdown: **Ibn ʿAbbās** is simultaneously narrated via `ʿIkrimah ← Hishām ibn Ḥassān` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3851](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3851), [3902](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3902)), `ʿAmr ibn Dīnār` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3903](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3903); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2351a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2351a)), and `Abū Jamrah al-Ḍubaʿī` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2351b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2351b)) as stating that the Prophet was commissioned at 40, received revelation in Mecca for **13 years**, stayed 10 years in Medina, and died at **age 63**. Yet as **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** documents in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (7/248, on *Bukhārī* 3902)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/7097/باب-هجرة-النبي-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-وأصحابه-إلى-المدينة), the identical core chain (`Ibn ʿAbbās ← ʿIkrimah ← Hishām ibn Ḥassān`, via Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān in *Musnad Aḥmad*) elsewhere narrates a **10-year** Meccan stay.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: فَمَكُثَ بِمَكَّةَ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً يُوحَى إِلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ أُمِرَ بِالْهِجْرَةِ فَهَاجَرَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ، وَمَاتَ وَهُوَ ابْنُ ثَلاَثٍ وَسِتِّينَ — "He stayed in Mecca thirteen years receiving revelation, then was commanded to migrate and migrated for ten years, and died when he was sixty-three" (Bukhārī 3902)

evidence_items.label: 15 Years in Mecca & Death at Age 65 (40 + 15 [7 + 8] + 10 = 65) via Ibn ʿAbbās
evidence_items.content_markdown: In five *ṣaḥīḥ* narrations via `ʿAmmār mawlā Banī Hāshim` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353a)–[2353e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353e); cf. [*Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī* 3650](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3650)), **Ibn ʿAbbās** asks his interlocutor, *"Do you know how to count (a-taḥsubu)?"* before dictating: *"Forty at which he was commissioned, fifteen in Mecca experiencing security and fear, and ten from his migration to Medina"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353a)–[2353b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353b)). He explicitly totals the Prophet's age at death to **65** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353c)–[2353d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353d)) and subdivides the 15-year Meccan stay into **7 years** of hearing voices and seeing light plus **8 years** of receiving revelation (`7 + 8 = 15`, [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353e)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: أَرْبَعِينَ بُعِثَ لَهَا خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ بِمَكَّةَ يَأْمَنُ وَيَخَافُ وَعَشْرَ مِنْ مُهَاجَرِه — "Do you know how to count? Forty at commissioning, fifteen in Mecca, and ten from his migration" (Muslim 2353a)

key_arabic_quote_structured.arabic: أَرْبَعِينَ بُعِثَ لَهَا خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ بِمَكَّةَ يَأْمَنُ وَيَخَافُ وَعَشْرَ مِنْ مُهَاجَرِه
key_arabic_quote_structured.english: Do you know how to count? Forty at commissioning, fifteen in Mecca, and ten from his migration

evidence_items.label: Classical Scholars Evaluating Narrator Oversight (Wahm) in the Age Reports
evidence_items.content_markdown: Evaluating the 10-, 13-, and 15-year reports in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (7/254)](https://shamela.ws/book/1673/4523) and [*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (15/105)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/4460/), **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** and **al-Nawawī** noted that where two counts from the same transmitter differ, one of the counts reflects narrator oversight (*wahm* or *ghalaṭ*).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ الصَّحِيحُ أَحَدَهُمَا — "Only one of the two conflicting counts can be authentic" (Fatḥ al-Bārī 6/659)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Traditional commentators sought to harmonize the 10-year Qurʾānic revelation reports in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4464](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4464) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4978](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4978) with the 13-year Meccan stay in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3902](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3902) either by appealing to rounding (*ilghāʾ al-kasr*), as discussed in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (8/620)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/9099/باب-كيف-نزل-الوحي-وأول-ما-نزل) and [*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (15/490)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/7014/باب-في-صفة-النبي-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-ومبعثه-وسنه), or by citing al-Shaʿbī's *mursal* report—recorded in **Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's** [*al-Istīʿāb* (1/36)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1080/14/عشيرته-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم) and graded authentic to al-Shaʿbī by **Ibn Kathīr** in [*al-Bidāyah wa-l-Nihāyah* (3/6)](https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9_%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AB%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AB/%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%87_%D8%B5%D9%84%D9%89_%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D9%87_%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%87_%D9%88%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%85_%D9%88%D9%82%D8%AA_%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AB%D8%AA%D9%87_%D9%88%D8%AA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%AE%D9%87%D8%A7)—that the angel Isrāfīl accompanied the Prophet for three years before Gabriel revealed the Qurʾān.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both **Ibn Ḥajar** ([*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 1/37](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/5/باب-بدء-الوحي); [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 12/376](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/12788/باب-أول-ما-بدئ-به-رسول-الله-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-من-الوحي-الرؤيا-الصالحة)) and **al-Suyūṭī** ([*al-Ḥāwī li-l-Fatāwī* 2/203](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/130/519/لبس-اليلب-في-الجواب-عن-إيراد-حلب)) rejected the Isrāfīl hypothesis as a disconnected (*mursal*) assertion that contradicts [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3). Moreover, as **Ibn Ḥajar** notes in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (7/758)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/8034/باب-وفاة-النبي-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم) and **al-Nawawī** notes in [*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (15/490)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/7014/باب-في-صفة-النبي-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-ومبعثه-وسنه), neither hypothesis reconciles the five *ṣaḥīḥ* chains in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353a)–[2353e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353e) dividing the Meccan stay into **7 + 8 = 15 years** (age 65).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Divergent Reports from Identical Key Sources
While chronological approximations are common in early historical records, the reports detailing the Prophet's age and Meccan stay present a specific textual challenge within Sunni authentication: they are transmitted as exact figures from the same primary authorities. **Ibn ʿAbbās** is recorded via various chains as stating that the Prophet stayed in Mecca for 13 years and died at 63 ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3902](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3902); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2351a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2351a)), for 10 years and died at 60 ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4978](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4978)), and for 15 years and died at 65 ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2353a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2353a)). **Anas ibn Mālik** is similarly recorded transmitting the 10-year stay and age 60 ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5900](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5900); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2347a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2347a)), while other reports via Anas state 63. The existence of three different authenticated timelines from the same key Companions prompted extensive classical evaluation of the mechanisms of oral preservation.

### 2. Classical Analysis and the Concept of Wahm
Classical commentators proposed several approaches to reconcile the different figures. A common harmonization suggested that the 10-year count omitted fractions or grouped the three years of clandestine preaching, while the 15-year count included the period between the initial vision and the formal commission. However, as **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** points out in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (7/254)](https://shamela.ws/book/1673/4523), these numerical adjustments cannot fully resolve the internal variants where the same transmitter explicitly provides differing counts.

Evaluating the textual tension, scholars such as **al-Nawawī** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 15/105](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/4460/)) and **Ibn Ḥajar** acknowledged that some narrators simply made errors in transmission (*wahm* or *ghalaṭ*). When addressing the 10-year count in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4978 from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Ḥajar states that only one of the two conflicting counts can be authentic, explicitly noting that the transmitter Hishām ibn Ḥassān erred (*wahm*). This scholarly acknowledgement illustrates how classical Hadith critics recognized human mnemonic lapse within the primary chains of the *Ṣaḥīḥayn*, reflecting their willingness to evaluate the substance of the text alongside the structural integrity of the *isnād*.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «بَعَثَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً، فَأَقَامَ بِمَكَّةَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ، وَبِالْمَدِينَةِ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ، وَتَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ سِتِّينَ سَنَةً، وَلَيْسَ فِي رَأْسِهِ وَلِحْيَتِهِ عِشْرُونَ شَعَرَةً بَيْضَاءَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"God commissioned him at the completion of forty years; he stayed in Mecca for ten years and in Medina for ten years, and God took him at the completion of sixty years, with scarcely twenty white hairs on his head and beard."*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ وَابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ قَالَا: لَبِثَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ يُنْزَلُ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ وَبِالْمَدِينَةِ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"From Abū Salamah, who said: ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās informed me; they both said: 'The Prophet ﷺ remained in Mecca for ten years while the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and in Medina for ten years.'"*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «بُعِثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً، فَمَكُثَ بِمَكَّةَ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً يُوحَى إِلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ أُمِرَ بِالْهِجْرَةِ فَهَاجَرَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ، وَمَاتَ وَهُوَ ابْنُ ثَلاَثٍ وَسِتِّينَ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"The Messenger of God ﷺ was commissioned at forty years of age, stayed in Mecca for thirteen years receiving revelation, then was commanded to migrate and lived as an emigrant for ten years, and died when he was sixty-three."*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «فَقَالَ [ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ]: أَتَحْسُبُ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: أَمْسِكْ: أَرْبَعِينَ بُعِثَ لَهَا، خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ بِمَكَّةَ يَأْمَنُ وَيَخَافُ، وَعَشْرَ مِنْ مُهَاجَرِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'Do you know how to count (a-taḥsubu)?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Hold fast to this: forty at which he was commissioned, fifteen [years] in Mecca experiencing security and fear, and ten [years] from his migration to Medina.'"*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «أَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً يَسْمَعُ الصَّوْتَ وَيَرَى الضَّوْءَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ وَلاَ يَرَى شَيْئًا وَثَمَانَ سِنِينَ يُوحَى إِلَيْهِ وَأَقَامَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ عَشْرًا»

subpoints.short_title: 3 Ṣaḥīḥ Reports Giving 4, 6 and 8 Bowings for One Eclipse Prayer
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see ʿĀʾishah's, Jābir's and Ibn ʿAbbās's reports of the eclipse prayer on the day Ibrāhīm died, and al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī and Ibn Taymiyyah judging the higher counts narrator error.
subpoints.takeaway: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī and Ibn Taymiyyah judged the higher counts in Muslim to be narrator error.
subpoints.title: Three Conflicting Bowing Counts in the Eclipse Prayer on the Day Ibrāhīm Died
subpoints.summary_markdown: Although the Medinan solar eclipse occurred on a single morning—the day the Prophet's son Ibrāhīm died (27 January 632 AD; [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c))—canonical eyewitness chains across the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* report three different counts of bowings (*rukūʿ*) for that public prayer: four ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901a)), six ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901f), [904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)), and eight ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 908](https://sunnah.com/muslim:908)–[909](https://sunnah.com/muslim:909)). Because competing *ṣaḥīḥ* narrations explicitly anchor their divergent counts to the day of Ibrāhīm's death ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)), classical Hadith scholars and jurists—including al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, al-Bukhārī, Ibn Taymiyyah ([*Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* 18:17–18](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/1773/فصل-قسمة-الحديث-إلى-صحيح-وحسن-وضعيف)), and Ibn al-Qayyim ([*Zād al-Maʿād* 1:436–439](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/127/94/فصل-في-هديه-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-في-صلاة-الكسوف))—concluded that the higher counts in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* reflect narrator error (*ghalaṭ*).

evidence_items.label: Three Reported Bowing Counts (4, 6, and 8) in Bukhārī and Muslim for the Eclipse Prayer
evidence_items.content_markdown: Canonical chains from **ʿĀʾishah** and **Ibn ʿAbbās** report **two bowings per *rakʿah* (four total)** on the day Ibrāhīm died ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901a), [901b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901b), [901c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901c), [901d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901d), [901e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901e)); parallel chains in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* from **ʿĀʾishah** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901f), [901g](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901g)) and **Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)) report **three bowings per *rakʿah* (six total)** explicitly dated to *"that very day when Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), died"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)); and a third strand in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* via `Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit ← Ṭāwūs ← Ibn ʿAbbās` reports **four bowings per *rakʿah* (eight total)** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 908](https://sunnah.com/muslim:908), [909](https://sunnah.com/muslim:909)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ فِي عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَ مَاتَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ابْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ النَّاسُ إِنَّمَا انْكَسَفَتْ لِمَوْتِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ‏.‏ فَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَصَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ بِأَرْبَعِ سَجَدَاتٍ — "The sun eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of God ﷺ, died... so the Prophet ﷺ stood and led the people in prayer with six bowings and four prostrations" (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 904c)

key_arabic_quote_structured.english: The sun eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of God ﷺ, died... so the Prophet ﷺ stood and led the people in prayer with six bowings and four prostrations

evidence_items.label: Classical Hadith Critics Identifying Narrator Error (Ghalaṭ) in the Multi-Bowing Reports of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim
evidence_items.content_markdown: **Ibn Taymiyyah** ([*Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* 18:17–18](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/1773/فصل-قسمة-الحديث-إلى-صحيح-وحسن-وضعيف); [24:254–262](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/3069/مسألة-الخسوف-والكسوف-لهما-أوقات-مقدرة)) cites Muslim's six-bowing ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)) and eight-bowing ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 908](https://sunnah.com/muslim:908)) eclipse narrations as primary examples of reports in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* whose chains are formally *ṣaḥīḥ* but whose texts contain transmitter error (`غَلَطٌ`) relative to the two-bowing report ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046)). Likewise, **Ibn al-Qayyim** ([*Zād al-Maʿād* 1:436–439](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/127/94/فصل-في-هديه-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-في-صلاة-الكسوف)) and **al-Shawkānī** ([*Nayl al-Awṭār* 3:391–392](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/47/1128/)) record that **Imām al-Shāfiʿī**, **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal**, and **al-Bukhārī** classified all counts exceeding two bowings per *rakʿah* in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* as errors by certain narrators (`غَلَطًا مِنْ بَعْضِ الرُّوَاةِ`).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّهُمَا لاَ يَنْخَسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلاَ لِحَيَاتِهِ — "The sun and the moon are among the signs of God, and they do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 901a)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators and jurists such as Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Khuzaymah, and al-Nawawī proposed harmonizing the divergent narrations by suggesting that the solar eclipse occurred multiple times in Medina during the Prophet's lifetime, and that he performed four bowings during one eclipse ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046)), six during another ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)), and eight during a third ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 908](https://sunnah.com/muslim:908)), as summarized in classical legal discussions ([*Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* 24:254–262](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/3069/مسألة-الخسوف-والكسوف-لهما-أوقات-مقدرة); [*Nayl al-Awṭār* 3:391–392](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/47/1128/)).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: However, primary-source analysis and classical critics such as **Ibn Taymiyyah** ([*Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* 18:17–18](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/1773/فصل-قسمة-الحديث-إلى-صحيح-وحسن-وضعيف); [24:254–262](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/3069/مسألة-الخسوف-والكسوف-لهما-أوقات-مقدرة)) and **Ibn al-Qayyim** ([*Zād al-Maʿād* 1:436–439](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/127/94/فصل-في-هديه-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-في-صلاة-الكسوف)) note that both the four-bowing report ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046)) and the six-bowing report ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)) explicitly anchor the prayer to *"the day Ibrāhīm died"* (`يَوْمَ مَاتَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ`), observing that *"Ibrāhīm did not die twice"* ([*Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* 18:17–18](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/1773/فصل-قسمة-الحديث-إلى-صحيح-وحسن-وضعيف)). Consequently, **al-Shāfiʿī**, **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal**, **al-Bukhārī**, **Ibn Taymiyyah**, and **Ibn al-Qayyim** concluded that the multiple-occasion hypothesis is incompatible with the explicit wording of the primary texts and that the higher counts in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* represent transmitter error (*ghalaṭ*) ([*Zād al-Maʿād* 1:436–439](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/127/94/فصل-في-هديه-صلى-الله-عليه-وسلم-في-صلاة-الكسوف)).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Divergent *Isnād* Branches for a Single Public Congregation
On the morning of 29 Shawwāl 10 AH (27 January 632 AD; NASA Eclipse Catalog #06259), an annular solar eclipse was visible over Medina on the exact day the Prophet's infant son **Ibrāhīm** passed away. The Prophet led a public two-*rakʿah* eclipse prayer (*ṣalāt al-kusūf*) in the mosque and delivered a sermon refuting the pre-Islamic belief that eclipses mark the birth or death of a human being. Despite the public visibility of those physical movements, canonical *isnāds* split into three ritual counts:
* **Four Bowings (Two per *Rakʿah*):** Transmitted in Medina via `ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr` and `ʿAmrah` from **ʿĀʾishah**, and via `ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār` from **Ibn ʿAbbās** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901a), [901e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901e)).
* **Six Bowings (Three per *Rakʿah*):** Transmitted in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* through the Meccan jurist `ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ` via `ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr ← ʿĀʾishah` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 901f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:901f)) and via `ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān ← ʿAṭāʾ ← Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh` ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)), where Jābir explicitly states that the sun eclipsed on the day Ibrāhīm died (*yawma māta Ibrāhīm*) and that the Prophet led the congregation in six bowings and four prostrations (*sitta rakaʿātin bi-arbaʿi sajadāt*).
* **Eight Bowings (Four per *Rakʿah*):** Transmitted via the Kūfan/Yemeni strand `Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit ← Ṭāwūs ← Ibn ʿAbbās` in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 908](https://sunnah.com/muslim:908) (cf. [909](https://sunnah.com/muslim:909)).

### 2. Classical Hadith Critics on the Multi-Eclipse Proposal
Jurists such as Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh and Ibn Khuzaymah proposed that the Prophet led multiple solar eclipse prayers on separate occasions using different bowing counts. However, **Ibn Taymiyyah** in *Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā* ([18:17–18](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/1773/), expanded at [24:254–262](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/22/3069/)) and **Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah** in *Zād al-Maʿād* ([1:436–439](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/127/94/)) demonstrated that the multi-eclipse hypothesis is refuted by the hadith texts themselves: both the two-bowing reports ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043), [1046](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1046)) and the three- and four-bowing reports ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 904c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:904c)) anchor the prayer to the morning Ibrāhīm died, and as Ibn Taymiyyah observed, *"Ibrāhīm did not die twice, nor did the Prophet have two sons named Ibrāhīm."* Summarizing the verdict of the early masters in *Nayl al-Awṭār* ([3:391–392](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/47/1128/)), **al-Shawkānī** and **Ibn al-Qayyim** record that **al-Shāfiʿī**, **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal**, and **al-Bukhārī** all rejected the 6- and 8-bowing variants in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* as transmitter errors (*ghalaṭan min baʿḍ al-ruwāt*). Such divergence over a single public liturgical observance indicates how the reports preserve differing descriptions of one prayer from one historical occasion.

subpoints.short_title: 3 Pilgrimage Modes and 2 Kaʿbah Accounts From the Prophet's One Hajj
subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see Companions in Bukhārī and Muslim describing the Farewell Pilgrimage as Ifrād, Tamattuʿ and Qirān, and Bilāl and Ibn ʿAbbās differing on whether he prayed inside the Kaʿbah.
subpoints.takeaway: Ṣaḥīḥ reports describe three pilgrimage modes; al-Nawawī attributed one Kaʿbah account to conjecture (ẓann).
subpoints.title: Eyewitness Contradictions on the Farewell Pilgrimage and Kaʿbah Prayer

subpoints.summary_markdown: In *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, eyewitness chains from Companions who accompanied the Prophet on his sole Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ*, 10 AH) attribute all three pilgrimage modes to him—*Ifrād* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1561](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1561)), *Tamattuʿ* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1691](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1691)), and *Qirān* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1232a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232a))—while Companions present simultaneously inside the locked Kaʿbah chamber give opposite testimonies on whether he prayed inside ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 397](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:397) vs. [398](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:398) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1330](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1330)). Classical commentators including **al-Nawawī** in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* ([8:302–305](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3505/), [9:449–450](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3911/)) and **al-ʿIrāqī** in *Ṭarḥ al-Tathrīb* ([5:19–25](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/310/1330/)) observed that reconciling these eyewitness accounts requires positing narrator conjecture (*ẓann*) or transmission error (*ghalaṭ*).

evidence_items.label: Divergent Eyewitness Accounts of the Mode of the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ifrād, Tamattuʿ, and Qirān)
evidence_items.content_markdown: Although the Prophet performed a single pilgrimage after the Hijrah (*Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ*, 10 AH), canonical reports from **ʿĀʾishah** state that he performed *Ifrād* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1561](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1561), [1562](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1562); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1211d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1211d), [1211h](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1211h)); reports from **Ibn ʿUmar** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1691](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1691); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1227](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1227)), an alternative transmission from **ʿĀʾishah** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1228](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1228)), and chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Abū Mūsā**, and **ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1564](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1564), [1571](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1571); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1222](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1222), [1226g](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1226g), [1240a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1240a)) report *Tamattuʿ*; and transmissions from **Anas ibn Mālik** and **ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1551](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1551), [1558](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1558), [1563](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1563), [4353](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4353); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1232a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232a), [1232b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232b)) state that he performed *Qirān*, with Anas remarking in response to Ibn ʿUmar's view: *"You treat us as nothing but mere children! I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'Labbayka ʿUmratan wa Ḥajjan'!"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1232a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232a)).

evidence_items.label: Divergent Eyewitness Accounts Inside the Closed Chamber of the Kaʿbah (Bilāl vs. Usāmah ibn Zayd and Ibn ʿAbbās)
evidence_items.content_markdown: When the Prophet entered the six-pillared interior chamber of the Kaʿbah accompanied by **Bilāl**, **Usāmah ibn Zayd**, and **ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah al-Ḥajabī** and closed the door, **Bilāl** reported upon exiting that the Prophet stood between the two front pillars and performed two *rakʿahs* of prayer inside ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 397](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:397), [468](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:468), [504](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:504), [1598](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1598); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1329a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1329a)). Conversely, **Ibn ʿAbbās** transmitted both directly ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 398](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:398), [1601](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1601); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1331](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1331)) and by explicitly citing **Usāmah ibn Zayd**, who was present inside the same chamber during the same visit ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1330](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1330)), that the Prophet supplicated in all its corners and **did not perform ritual prayer inside it** before exiting.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 8:302–305](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3505/باب-بيان-وجوه-الإحرام-وأنه-يجوز-إفراد-الحج-والتمتع-والقران), [9:449–450](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3911/باب-استحباب-دخول-الكعبة-للحاج-وغيره-والصلاة-فيها-والدعاء-في-نواحيها-كلها)) proposed harmonizing the Kaʿbah interior reports by applying the juristic principle that an affirmative report (*muthbit*) takes precedence over a negative one (*nāfī*), suggesting that Usāmah ibn Zayd was occupied in another part of the dimly lit chamber and did not observe the Prophet's prayer. Regarding the Farewell Pilgrimage, commentators suggested that the Prophet initially entered *iḥrām* for *Ḥajj* alone (*Ifrād*) and subsequently integrated *ʿUmrah* into it (*Qirān*), or that individual Companions applied the terms *Ifrād*, *Tamattuʿ*, and *Qirān* to different aspects of his ritual actions and instructions.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Primary-source analysis and classical commentators note that reconciling these accounts still requires attributing conjecture or transmission error to specific links in the *ṣaḥīḥ* chains. In the Kaʿbah account, Usāmah ibn Zayd explicitly reported observing the Prophet supplicate in *"all its corners"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1330](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1330); cf. [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 398](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:398)), leading **al-Nawawī** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 9:449–450](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3911/باب-استحباب-دخول-الكعبة-للحاج-وغيره-والصلاة-فيها-والدعاء-في-نواحيها-كلها)) to explain that Usāmah reported the negation on the basis of personal conjecture (`عَمَلًا بِظَنِّهِ`) rather than comprehensive observation. Similarly, regarding the Farewell Pilgrimage, **al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ** ([*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 8:302–305](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3505/باب-بيان-وجوه-الإحرام-وأنه-يجوز-إفراد-الحج-والتمتع-والقران)) and **Walī al-Dīn al-ʿIrāqī** ([*Ṭarḥ al-Tathrīb* 5:19–25](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/310/1330/حديث-أن-رسول-الله-أفرد-الحج)) noted that several harmonization proposals involved strained interpretation (*mutakallif*) and recorded that early authorities faulted Hishām ibn ʿUrwah for *tadlīs* and regarded **ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr's** transmission from ʿĀʾishah regarding her *iḥrām* for *ʿUmrah* during the Farewell Pilgrimage as a narrator error (`وَغَلَّطُوا عُرْوَةَ فِي الْعُمْرَةِ`).

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Three Competing Eyewitness Traditions on the Farewell Pilgrimage Mode
During his post-Hijrah life, the Prophet performed only one *Ḥajj* (*Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ*, Dhū al-Ḥijjah 10 AH), pronouncing his ritual intention (*Talbiyah*) aloud from the *mīqāt* of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah before tens of thousands of followers. Nevertheless, canonical eyewitness chains split across all three juristic categories of pilgrimage—and also differ across chains within transmissions from the same Companion:
* ***Ifrād* (*Ḥajj* Alone):** Transmitted from **ʿĀʾishah** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1561](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1561), [1562](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1562); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1211d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1211d), [1211h](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1211h)), **Ibn ʿUmar**, and **Jābir**, forming the evidentiary basis of the Mālikī and Shāfiʿī schools.
* ***Tamattuʿ* (*ʿUmrah* Interrupted by *Taḥallul*, Then *Ḥajj*):** Transmitted via competing chains from **Ibn ʿUmar** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1691](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1691); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1227](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1227)) and **ʿĀʾishah** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1228](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1228)), alongside several other leading Companions ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1564](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1564), supplemented by [1571](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1571); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1222](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1222), [1226g](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1226g), and [1240a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1240a)).
* ***Qirān* (Conjoined *ʿUmrah* and *Ḥajj* Without Exiting *Iḥrām*):** Transmitted from **Anas ibn Mālik**, **ʿAlī**, and **ʿUmar** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 1551](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1551), [1558](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1558)–[1559](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1559), and [1563](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1563); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1232a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232a), [1232b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1232b)), where Anas rebukes Ibn ʿUmar's *Ifrād* claim by insisting he personally heard the Prophet chant both rites together.

In *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* ([8:302–305](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3505/)) and *Ṭarḥ al-Tathrīb* ([5:19–25](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/310/1330/)), **al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ**, **al-Nawawī**, and **Zayn al-Dīn al-ʿIrāqī** highlight the epistemological problem: because the pilgrimage was a single event (*ḥajjah wāḥidah*) reported from direct visual and auditory observation (*mushāhadah*), reconciling all chains requires strained contrivance (*takalluf*), while early critics explicitly faulted `ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr` for erring in his pilgrimage transmission from ʿĀʾishah (*wa-ghallaṭū ʿUrwah fī al-ʿumrah*).

### 2. Opposite Eyewitness Verdicts Inside the Locked Kaʿbah Chamber
A parallel eyewitness divergence occurs inside the enclosed interior of the Kaʿbah, where the Prophet entered accompanied only by Bilāl, Usāmah, and ʿUthmān behind a locked door. Upon stepping out, **Bilāl** affirmed to Ibn ʿUmar ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 397](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:397), [468](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:468), and [1598](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1598); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1329a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1329a)) that the Prophet prayed two *rakʿahs* between the two southern pillars. Yet **Usāmah ibn Zayd**—standing inside that same small room during the exact same minutes—testified via **Ibn ʿAbbās** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1330](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1330)), alongside Ibn ʿAbbās's direct transmissions ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 398](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:398), [1601](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1601); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1331](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1331)), that the Prophet only supplicated (*daʿā*) in the corners and did not perform ritual prayer (`وَلَمْ يُصَلِّ فِيهِ`) until exiting the building. In *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* ([9:449–450](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/3911/)), **al-Nawawī** could preserve both reports only by suggesting that Usāmah issued an unqualified negative testimony based on personal supposition (`عَمَلًا بِظَنِّهِ`) while distracted in a dim corner.

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «مَا تَعُدُّونَنَا إِلَّا صِبْيَانًا! سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً وَحَجًّا»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"You treat us as nothing but mere children! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: 'Labbayka ʿUmratan wa Ḥajjan'!"*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «فَإِنْ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ وَقَعَ الِاخْتِلَافُ بَيْنَ الصَّحَابَةِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ فِي صِفَةِ حَجَّتِهِ ﷺ وَهِيَ حَجَّةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ يُخْبِرُ عَنْ مُشَاهَدَةٍ فِي قَضِيَّةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ؟ قَالَ الْقَاضِي عِيَاضٌ: قَدْ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسُ الْكَلَامَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْأَحَادِيثِ، فَمِنْ مُجِيدٍ مُنْصِفٍ، وَمِنْ مُقَصِّرٍ مُتَكَلِّفٍ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"If it is asked: How did disagreement occur among the Companions regarding the description of his ﷺ Ḥajj, when it was a single Ḥajj and each one of them was reporting from eyewitness observation (mushāhadah) of a single event? Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: 'People have spoken at great length regarding these hadiths—some doing well and being fair, and some falling short and resorting to strained contrivance (mutakallif)...'"*

arabic_blockquotes.arabic_text: «أَخْبَرَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ لَمَّا دَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ دَعَا فِي نَوَاحِيهِ كُلِّهَا وَلَمْ يُصَلِّ فِيهِ حَتَّى خَرَجَ فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ رَكَعَ فِي قُبُلِ الْبَيْتِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَقَالَ هَذِهِ الْقِبْلَةُ»
arabic_blockquotes.english_translation: *"Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me that when the Prophet ﷺ entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners, and he did not pray in it (wa-lam yuṣalli fīhi) until he came out; when he came out, he prayed two rakʿahs facing the front of the House and said: 'This is the Qiblah.'"*

subpoints.plain_english_hook: Here you'll see reports naming Sūrah 96, Sūrah 74 or a sūrah on Paradise and the Fire as the first, and two verses and two sūrahs as the last, with the explanations commentators offered.
subpoints.takeaway: Ṣaḥīḥ reports name different first and last revelations; al-Nawawī judged Jābir's literal claim weak.
subpoints.title: Conflicting Ṣaḥīḥ Reports on the First and Last Qurʾānic Revelations
subpoints.summary_markdown: Canonical chains in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* transmit three different accounts of the absolute first Qurʾānic revelation (*awwal mā nazala*): *Sūrat al-ʿAlaq* ([Qurʾān 96:1–5](https://quran.com/96/1-5)) in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3), *Sūrat al-Muddaththir* ([Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5)) in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4922](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4922) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161d), and a *Mufaṣṣal* *sūrah* mentioning Paradise and the Fire in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4993](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4993). Parallel *ṣaḥīḥ* chains likewise diverge without qualification over the final revelation (*ākhir mā nazala*), identifying it variously as the Verse of *Ribā* ([Qurʾān 2:278–281](https://quran.com/2/278-281); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4544](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4544)), the Verse of *Kalālah* ([Qurʾān 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)) and *Sūrat Barāʾah* ([Qurʾān 9](https://quran.com/9); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4605](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4605)), or *Sūrat al-Naṣr* ([Qurʾān 110:1–3](https://quran.com/110/1-3); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3024a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3024a)).

evidence_items.label: Three Ṣaḥīḥ Accounts of the First Revelation (Q. 96:1–5, Q. 74:1–5, and a Mufaṣṣal Sūrah)
evidence_items.content_markdown: While **ʿĀʾishah** (`← ʿUrwah ← al-Zuhrī`) identifies *Sūrat al-ʿAlaq* ([Qurʾān 96:1–5](https://quran.com/96/1-5)) as the first revelation in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3), [4953](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4953), [4955](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4955), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 160a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:160a), **Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh** (`← Abū Salamah ← Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr`) in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4922](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4922), [4924](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4924), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161d) explicitly rejects the *Iqraʾ* ([Qurʾān 96:1–5](https://quran.com/96/1-5)) identification and testifies from the Prophet that the very first revelation of the Qurʾān (`أَوَّلِ مَا نَزَلَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ`) was *Sūrat al-Muddaththir* ([Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5)). Meanwhile, a second *ṣaḥīḥ* chain from **ʿĀʾishah** (`← Yūsuf ibn Māhak ← Ibn Jurayj`) in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4993](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4993) states that the very first revelation (`أَوَّلَ مَا نَزَلَ مِنْهُ`) was *"a sūrah from al-Mufaṣṣal in which there is mention of Paradise and the Fire"* (`سُورَةٌ مِنَ الْمُفَصَّلِ فِيهَا ذِكْرُ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ`)—whereas neither [Qurʾān 96:1–5](https://quran.com/96/1-5) (nor the entirety of [Qurʾān 96:1–19](https://quran.com/96/1-19)) nor [Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5) contains any mention of Paradise (*al-Jannah*).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ لاَ أُحَدِّثُكَ إِلاَّ مَا حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ — "Jābir said: I will only narrate to you what the Messenger of God ﷺ narrated to us" (Bukhārī 4922)

evidence_items.label: Ṣaḥīḥ Reports on the Final Verse (Q. 2:278–281 vs. Q. 4:176) and Final Sūrah (Q. 9 vs. Q. 110)
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4544](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4544), **Ibn ʿAbbās** (`← al-Shaʿbī`) states without qualification that *"the last verse revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was the Verse of Ribā"* ([Qurʾān 2:278–281](https://quran.com/2/278-281); cf. ʿUmar's report in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3032a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3032a)). Conversely, in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4364](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4364), [4605](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4605), [4654](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4654), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1618a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1618a)–[1618b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1618b), **al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib** (`← Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī`) states that the last verse revealed was the Verse of *Kalālah* ([Qurʾān 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)) and the last *sūrah* revealed was *Barāʾah* ([Qurʾān 9](https://quran.com/9))—while **Ibn ʿAbbās** (`← ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh`) in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3024a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3024a)–[3024b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3024b) identifies the last complete *sūrah* revealed as *Sūrat al-Naṣr* ([Qurʾān 110:1–3](https://quran.com/110/1-3)).
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: آخِرُ آيَةٍ نَزَلَتْ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم آيَةُ الرِّبَا — "The last verse revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was the Verse of Ribā" (Bukhārī 4544)

Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4605 (Q. 4:176 as last verse and Q. 9 as last sūrah via al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators—such as **Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī** in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (8/620, on *Bukhārī* 4978)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/9099/باب-كيف-نزل-الوحي-وأول-ما-نزل) and [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (8/558, on *Bukhārī* 4922)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/8956/باب-قوله-وربك-فكبر) and **Imām al-Nawawī** in [*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (2/205–207, on *Muslim* 160–161)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/473/)—propose that Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (drawing on al-Zuhrī's transmission in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161a)) intended only that [Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5) was the first revelation after the temporary pause in revelation (*fatrat al-waḥy*) or the first command to warn publicly. Similarly, regarding the final revelation, **Ibn Ḥajar** in [*Fatḥ al-Bārī* (8/206, on *Bukhārī* 4544)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/8180/باب-واتقوا-يوما-ترجعون-فيه-إلى-الله) suggests that competing 'last verse' reports reflect relative finality on a specific legal subject (such as commercial usury in [Qurʾān 2:278–281](https://quran.com/2/278-281) or collateral inheritance in [Qurʾān 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)) or what each Companion personally heard last based on individual inference (*ijtihād*).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In the transmission of Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr from Abū Salamah in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4922](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4922) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161d), Jābir is explicitly asked whether *Iqraʾ* ([Qurʾān 96:1–5](https://quran.com/96/1-5)) was the absolute first revelation of the Qurʾān (`أَوَّلِ مَا نَزَلَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ`) and rejects that view in favor of *Sūrat al-Muddaththir* ([Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5)), prompting **al-Nawawī** in [*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (2/206)](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/473/) to classify the literal import of Jābir's statement as weak or invalid (`ضَعِيفٌ بَلْ بَاطِلٌ`). Moreover, neither account aligns with ʿĀʾishah's separate *ṣaḥīḥ* report in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4993](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4993) that the very first revelation (`أَوَّلَ مَا نَزَلَ مِنْهُ`) was a *Mufaṣṣal* *sūrah* mentioning Paradise and the Fire. Likewise, [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4544](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4544) ([Qurʾān 2:278–281](https://quran.com/2/278-281)) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1618a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1618a) ([Qurʾān 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)) both employ the unqualified superlative `آخِرُ آيَةٍ نَزَلَتْ` (*"the last verse revealed"*), an observation reflecting Ibn Ḥajar's note (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 8/206) that *ṣaḥīḥ* chains may transmit subjective Companion inference (*ijtihād*) in the linguistic form of definitive historical testimony.

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Transmission Analysis of the Three *Awwal Mā Nazala* Traditions
Rather than converging on a single memory of how scriptural revelation began, the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* preserve three distinct regional and family chains:
* **The `al-Zuhrī ← ʿUrwah ← ʿĀʾishah` Strand (*Sūrat al-ʿAlaq*):** Recorded in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3) (with parallels in [4953](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4953), [6982](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6982), and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 160a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:160a)), this narrative identifies the opening five verses of [Qurʾān 96](https://quran.com/96/1-5) as the initial revelation at Cave Ḥirāʾ. Because ʿĀʾishah was born roughly seven years after the call, her report is a Companion *mursal* (*mursal al-ṣaḥābī*).
* **The `Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr ← Abū Salamah ← Jābir` Strand (*Sūrat al-Muddaththir*):** Recorded in [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4922](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4922) (alongside [4924](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4924) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161d)), this dialogue directly confronts and rejects the *Iqraʾ* claim. When Yaḥyā objects that people consider *Iqraʾ* the earliest revelation, Abū Salamah recounts putting that exact question to **Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh**, who insisted on narrating directly from the Prophet that his seclusion at Ḥirāʾ culminated in the revelation of [Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5). Commentators sought to subordinate Jābir's testimony by appealing to al-Zuhrī's variant from Abū Salamah ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 161a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:161a)), which inserts a pause (*fatrat al-waḥy*) before *al-Muddaththir*; yet because `Yaḥyā ← Abū Salamah` explicitly repudiates the priority of *Iqraʾ*, **al-Nawawī** in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* ([2:206](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/53/473/)) pronounced Jābir's deduction weak and invalid (`ضَعِيفٌ بَلْ بَاطِلٌ`).
* **The `Ibn Jurayj ← Yūsuf ibn Māhak ← ʿĀʾishah` Strand (*Al-Mufaṣṣal*):** In [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4993](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4993), a Meccan chain from ʿĀʾishah states that the earliest revelation was a short *Mufaṣṣal* chapter depicting both Paradise (*al-Jannah*) and Hellfire—a description incompatible with [Qurʾān 96](https://quran.com/96/1-19) and [Qurʾān 74:1–5](https://quran.com/74/1-5), neither of which mentions Paradise.

### 2. Unqualified Superlatives on the Final Revelation (*Ākhir Mā Nazala*)
The same divergence recurs at the close of revelation, where authentic chains employ absolute superlative phrasing (`آخِرُ آيَةٍ` / `آخِرُ سُورَةٍ`) without topical restriction:
* **Ibn ʿAbbās via `al-Shaʿbī`** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4544](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4544)) designates the *Ribā* passage ([Qurʾān 2:278–281](https://quran.com/2/278-281)), matching ʿUmar's statement ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3032a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3032a)) that the Prophet died before expounding it.
* **Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib via `Abū Isḥāq`** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4364](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4364), [4605](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4605); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1618a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1618a)) names [Qurʾān 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176) (*Kalālah*) as the last verse and [Qurʾān 9](https://quran.com/9) (*Barāʾah*, revealed in 9 AH) as the last chapter.
* **Ibn ʿAbbās via `ʿUbayd Allāh`** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3024a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3024a)) names *Sūrat al-Naṣr* ([Qurʾān 110:1–3](https://quran.com/110/1-3)), whereas **Ibn ʿAbbās via `Saʿīd ibn Jubayr`** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4590](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4590); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3023a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3023a)) names the verse of intentional homicide ([Qurʾān 4:93](https://quran.com/4/93)), and **ʿUmar** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 45](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:45); [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3017a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:3017a)) anchors [Qurʾān 5:3](https://quran.com/5/3) to the Farewell Pilgrimage at ʿArafah. As **Ibn Ḥajar** notes in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* ([8:206](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/52/8180/باب-واتقوا-يوما-ترجعون-فيه-إلى-الله)), each Companion reported the final verse according to personal knowledge rather than a unified canonical register.

subpoints.summary_markdown: Within a single chapter of *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (*Kitāb al-Nikāḥ*, [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c)–[1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1407a)), four eyewitness Companions transmit four different timelines for the prohibition of temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*). Authenticated chains diverge over whether the Prophet banned *mutʿah* at Khaybar in 7 AH ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1407a); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4216](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4216)), at the Conquest of Mecca in Ramadan 8 AH ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f), [1406j](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406j)), or at Awṭās in Shawwāl 8 AH ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f)), or whether Companions practiced it openly throughout the Prophet's lifetime and Abū Bakr's caliphate until Caliph ʿUmar prohibited it ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)).

evidence_items.label: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh's Testimony That Companions Practiced Mutʿah Until Caliph ʿUmar Prohibited It
evidence_items.content_markdown: In [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d), **Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh** reports no prophetic prohibition during the Prophet's lifetime, testifying instead that the Companions contracted temporary marriage *"for a handful of dates or flour during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and during the time of Abū Bakr until ʿUmar forbade it in the case of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)).

evidence_items.content_markdown: In contrast to Jābir's testimony ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c)–[1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)), **ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib** dates the prophetic prohibition to the campaign of Khaybar in 7 AH ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1407a); [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4216](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4216)); **Sabrah ibn Maʿbad al-Juhanī** reports that the Prophet permitted *mutʿah* at the Conquest of Mecca in 8 AH before prohibiting it before they left Mecca ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f)), declaring it forbidden *"until the Day of Resurrection"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406d)) while standing between the Corner and the door of the Kaʿbah ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406e)), after a marriage was contracted for two red cloaks ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406a), [1406j](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406j)); and **Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ** places its prophetic permission and subsequent prohibition later in 8 AH during the campaign of Awṭās following the Conquest of Mecca ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f)).

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators, beginning with Imām Muslim's chapter heading for [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c–1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c) and later expositors, proposed harmonizing the four accounts through a sequence of repeated abrogations (*naskh*): positing that *mutʿah* was prohibited at Khaybar ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1407a)), re-permitted and prohibited at the Conquest of Mecca ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f), [1406j](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406j)), and re-permitted and prohibited at Awṭās ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f)), while Companions such as Jābir ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c)–[1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)) remained unaware of the prophetic prohibitions until ʿUmar's caliphate.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: However, primary-source analysis notes that in Sabrah's transmissions ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406d), [1406e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406e), [1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f)), the Prophet prohibited *mutʿah* at the Conquest of Mecca and declared that God forbade it **"until the Day of Resurrection"** (`إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ`), which is textually incompatible with a subsequent prophetic concession weeks later at Awṭās ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f)). Moreover, as Imām al-Shāfiʿī observed, no other legal ruling in Islam underwent repeated cycles of abrogation and re-permission, nor does repeated abrogation explain how Medinan Companions practiced *mutʿah* openly throughout the entire caliphate of Abū Bakr ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c)–[1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)) without any prophetic prohibition being enforced.

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Four Reported Timelines in Kitāb al-Nikāḥ
Public prohibitions of marriage practices during military campaigns directly regulated the conduct of thousands of soldiers. Yet in a single chapter of *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (*Kitāb al-Nikāḥ*), four authenticated eyewitness chains assign the prohibition of temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) to four different historical settings:
* **The Khaybar Prohibition (Muḥarram 7 AH / 628 AD):** Transmitted via `al-Zuhrī ← ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan (sons of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah) ← ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib` in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1407a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1407a) and [*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4216](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4216), where ʿAlī rebukes Ibn ʿAbbās by stating that the Prophet prohibited both temporary marriage with women and the meat of domestic donkeys on the Day of Khaybar (`يَوْمَ خَيْبَرَ`).
* **The Perpetual Meccan Prohibition (Ramadan 8 AH / Jan 630 AD):** Transmitted via `al-Rabīʿ ibn Sabrah ← Sabrah ibn Maʿbad al-Juhanī` across [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406a), [1406d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406d), [1406e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406e), [1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f), and [1406j](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406j), where Sabrah recounts contracting a temporary marriage for two red cloaks during the Conquest of Mecca before the Prophet stood between the *Rukn* and the Door of the Kaʿbah and declared *mutʿah* forbidden perpetually *"until the Day of Resurrection"* (*ilā yawm al-qiyāmah*).
* **The Awṭās Concession and Ban (Shawwāl 8 AH / Feb 630 AD):** Transmitted via `Iyās ibn Salamah ← Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ` in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f), which places a fresh three-day prophetic permission and subsequent prohibition in the Year of Awṭās (`عَامَ أَوْطَاسٍ`)—weeks after the Conquest of Mecca, where Sabrah's chain claimed *mutʿah* had already been banned until Resurrection Day.
* **Uninterrupted Practice Until Caliph ʿUmar's Ban (13–23 AH):** Transmitted via `Abū al-Zubayr` and `ʿAṭāʾ` from **Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh** in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405c) and [1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d), where Jābir testifies that Medinan Companions continued contracting *mutʿah* for a handful of dates and flour throughout the entire lifetime of the Prophet and the caliphate of Abū Bakr (*ʿalā ʿahdi Rasūli Llāhi ﷺ wa-Abī Bakr*), until Caliph ʿUmar prohibited it following the case of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth.

### 2. Classical Discussion of Repeated Abrogation (Naskh)
To reconcile all four reports, Imām Muslim's chapter heading and commentators such as **al-Nawawī** and **al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ** proposed that *mutʿah* was permitted and abrogated twice—or up to six times—across additional expeditions including *ʿUmrat al-Qaḍāʾ*, Tabūk, and the Farewell Pilgrimage. However, **Imām al-Shāfiʿī** noted that no other precept in Islamic law ever underwent repeated cycles of abrogation and re-authorization, while **Ibn al-Qayyim** and **Ibn Ḥajar** observed that a perpetual ban (*ilā yawm al-qiyāmah*) proclaimed at the Kaʿbah ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1406d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406d), [1406f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1406f)) cannot logically precede a fresh prophetic concession during the Awṭās campaign ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405f](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405f)) or open practice in Medina under Abū Bakr ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1405d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1405d)).

subpoints.summary_markdown: Although the Farewell Sermon (*Khuṭbat al-Wadāʿ*, 10 AH) was delivered publicly before more than 10,000 Companions, canonical transmissions in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* split between bequeathing **"the Book of Allah" alone** at ʿArafāt ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a); cf. [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 1905](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1905)) and **"two weighty things: the Book of Allah... and the people of my household (Ahl al-Bayt)"** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2408a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2408a); cf. [*Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī* 3786](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3786)). By contrast, the familiar juristic pairing **"the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet"** is entirely absent from *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī*, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, and all Six Canonical Books, entering [*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 46/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:46/3) solely as an unchained report (*balāgh*).

evidence_items.label: Canonical Split Between 'The Book of Allah' Alone (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1218a) and 'The Book of Allah and My Household' (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2408a; cf. Tirmidhī 3786)
evidence_items.content_markdown: In the longest canonical narrative of the Farewell Pilgrimage via `Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ← Muḥammad al-Bāqir ← Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq ← Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl`, the Prophet's address on the Day of ʿArafāt specifies a single written authority: ***"the Book of Allah"* alone** ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a); [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 1905](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1905)). Conversely, in **Zayd ibn Arqam's** canonical Ghadīr Khumm narration in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2408a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2408a), the Prophet declares that he is leaving behind ***"two weighty things (thaqalayn): the first of them is the Book of Allah... and the people of my household (Ahl al-Bayt),"*** while a competing branch of the **identical three early links** (`Jābir ← al-Bāqir ← Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq`) in [*Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī* 3786](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3786) places ***"the Book of Allah and my family (ʿitratī ahl baytī)"*** directly in the ʿArafāt sermon atop his she-camel al-Qaṣwāʾ.
