evidence_items.label: The Ṣaḥīḥayn Bequest of 'Two Weighty Things' (Muslim 2408a) vs. the Absence of 'Book and Sunnah' From All Six Canonical Books
evidence_items.content_markdown: Whereas *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* authenticates both *"the Book of Allah"* alone ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a)) and the *thaqalayn* pairing of *"the Book of Allah... and the people of my household"* ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2408a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2408a)), the popular juristic formula *"the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet"* (*Kitāb Allāh wa-Sunnat Nabiyyihi*) is **entirely absent from *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī*, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, and all Six Canonical Books**. Its earliest legal citation in Mālik ibn Anas's *Muwaṭṭaʾ* ([*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 46/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:46/3)) appears **without any chain of transmission (*isnād*)** as an unattributed report (`أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ`, *"that it reached him"*), acquiring secondary connected chains only in later non-canonical compilations.
evidence_items.key_arabic_quote: وَأَنَا تَارِكٌ فِيكُمْ ثَقَلَيْنِ أَوَّلُهُمَا كِتَابُ اللَّهِ فِيهِ الْهُدَى وَالنُّورُ فَخُذُوا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَاسْتَمْسِكُوا بِهِ — "And I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of God, in which is guidance and light—so take hold of the Book of God and adhere to it... and the people of my household (Ahl al-Bayt)." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2408a)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators proposed that the Prophet delivered multiple addresses during the Farewell Pilgrimage and the return journey—speaking on the Day of ʿArafāt ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a)), at Minā, and subsequently at Ghadīr Khumm ([*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2408a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2408a))—emphasizing adherence to 'the Book of Allah' at one location, 'my Ahl al-Bayt' at another, and 'the Sunnah of His Prophet' ([*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 46/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:46/3)) at a third.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: However, primary-source analysis indicates that both [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a) (*"the Book of Allah"* alone) and [*Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī* 3786](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3786) (*"the Book of Allah and my family"*) are transmitted through the **identical early family *isnād*** (`Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ← Muḥammad al-Bāqir ← Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq`) and explicitly describe the **same sermon on the Day of ʿArafāt** delivered atop his she-camel al-Qaṣwāʾ (`يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ وَهُوَ عَلَى نَاقَتِهِ الْقَصْوَاءِ يَخْطُبُ`), indicating textual divergence in the transmission of a single address. Meanwhile, the juristic *"and the Sunnah of His Prophet"* formula in [*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 46/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:46/3) circulated without an *isnād* (*balāgh*) in the second century AH and was omitted by both *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*.

subpoints.deep_dive_markdown:
### 1. Bifurcation of the `Jābir ← al-Bāqir ← al-Ṣādiq` Family *Isnād*
In classical Hadith theory, a constitutional address delivered before tens of thousands of pilgrims on the Day of ʿArafāt (9 Dhū al-Ḥijjah 10 AH) represents the prime candidate for mass, uniform transmission (*tawātur*). Instead, the primary canonical narrative of the Farewell Sermon descends through a single Medinan family stem—`Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (d. 148 AH) ← his father Muḥammad al-Bāqir (d. 114 AH) ← Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (d. 78 AH)`—which bifurcates immediately below Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq into two distinct wordings:
* **The Medinan Recension of Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl (*Book of Allah Alone*):** Recorded in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1218a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1218a) and [*Sunan Abī Dāwūd* 1905](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1905), this branch transmits the complete itinerary of the Prophet's pilgrimage and quotes his sermon at ʿArafāt as leaving behind a single authoritative safeguard against error: **the Book of Allah** (`كِتَابُ اللَّهِ`), without mentioning either the *Ahl al-Bayt* or a separate corpus of *Sunnah*.
* **The Kūfan Recension of Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan al-Anmāṭī (*Book of Allah and My Family*):** Recorded in [*Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī* 3786](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3786) (graded *ḥasan gharīb*), this branch shares the exact same `Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq ← Muḥammad al-Bāqir ← Jābir` stem and explicitly places the scene on the Day of ʿArafāt atop his she-camel al-Qaṣwāʾ (*yawma ʿArafata wa-huwa ʿalā nāqatihi al-Qaṣwāʾi yakhṭubu*), and records the dual bequest of **the Book of Allah and my family (`عِتْرَتِي أَهْلَ بَيْتِي`)**. Because both recensions specify the identical ʿArafāt setting atop al-Qaṣwāʾ, commentators cannot separate them by appealing to the later homeward halt at Ghadīr Khumm (18 Dhū al-Ḥijjah 10 AH) narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam in [*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2408a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2408a).

### 2. Absence of the *"Book and Sunnah"* Formula from the *Ṣaḥīḥayn*
The third version—bequeathing *"the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet"* (`كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةَ نَبِيِّهِ`)—is absent from all Six Canonical Books (*al-Kutub al-Sittah*). Its earliest appearance in [*Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik* 46/3](https://sunnah.com/malik:46/3) is a chainless report (*balāgh*: *balaghahu anna Rasūla Llāhi ﷺ qāla*) separated from 10 AH by more than a century. Only in later compilations (such as al-Ḥākim's *Mustadrak* and al-Bayhaqī's *Sunan*) was this formula equipped with complete chains through weak intermediates (`Ṣāliḥ ibn Mūsā al-Ṭalḥī`, `Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways`, and `Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh`), whom classical *rijāl* critics including al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Ḥajar condemned as abandoned (*matrūk*) or pillars of falsehood. Across these early and canonical collections, the Farewell Sermon bequest is preserved in three distinct wordings: 'the Book of Allah' alone, 'the Book of Allah and the people of my household,' and 'the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet.'
